# commentable-html feature specification

commentable-html turns a standalone HTML artifact into a self-contained code-review surface. A reader can select text, code, diff lines, mermaid nodes or whole diagrams, headings, images, and charts, leave comments in the page, copy a machine-readable review bundle back to an agent, and let the agent mark processed comments handled in the same HTML file.

The core invariant is self-contained operation. Standalone mode embeds the CSS, state blocks, UI, and runtime in one file. NonShareable mode keeps the document-owned state inline but loads CSS and JS from local companion files in `dist/`; its export action rebuilds one shareable file so the review can travel without companions. The review layer is bundled into the document. Optional host features, such as mermaid rendering, Chart.js, tooltip libraries, and Run in Azure Data Explorer links, can load from a CDN and should be vendored, inlined, or captured with Export Offline when single-file zero-network shareability is required.

Current UI label note: the authoritative action label is `Export as Shareable`. Some historical test names still say `Save comments`, `Save in HTML`, or `Export with embedded comments`.

Coverage notation: each row lists the strongest automated coverage or source citation I found. `manual/validator` means the behavior is a documented convention or a static validator invariant rather than a browser E2E behavior test.

This is a denial-of-affordance guard, not a privilege boundary. | `tests/09-interactions.spec.js` - `CMH-CORE-21: an author element wearing a layer control's class does not suppress the real control`, `CMH-CORE-21: an author element that spoofs a control class gains nothing and is still swallowed`, `CMH-CORE-21: expanding a collapsed section from the sidebar restamps the layer's own caret`; source: `assets/js/00-preamble.js` - `cmhOwnChrome`, `assets/js/62-sortable-tables.js`, `assets/js/82-toc.js`, `assets/js/84-section-review.js`, `assets/js/35-widgets.js`, `assets/js/50-sidebar.js` |

| CMH-CORE-24 | The composer's drag grip (`.cm-composer-handle .grip`) is DRAWN, never typeset. It used to be a pair of `U+22EE` glyphs in a `line-height: 1` box, so it went through the font pipeline - fallback resolution, the glyph cache, and a text origin snapped to whole device pixels from a font-metric-derived baseline that measured OFF the device grid - and it landed one CSS pixel higher or lower between two otherwise identical renders of the same page in the same digest-pinned container. The exact drift budget (`MAX_DIFF_PIXELS` 0, CMH-BUILD-19) is unchanged, because the rendering was fixed rather than the gate widened; the precise input that varied between two runs was never reproduced on a quiet host (six sequential and twelve concurrent captures were byte-identical), so the fix removes the whole text-rendering pipeline from the element instead of chasing it. The grip is now a definite 6x10 box carrying six `currentColor` dots painted from its own geometry, so there is no glyph to rasterize and therefore no font fallback, glyph cache or text-origin snapping in the element at all: its SIZE and the SHAPE it draws are the same whatever font stack resolves for the surrounding chrome. Its PLACEMENT is still the flex line's business - the `drag to move` label beside it sets the line's cross size and the grip is centred in it, so a font change on the HANDLE re-centres it and re-antialiases the circles at their new sub-pixel offset (the covering test pins the box and the painted ink there, not the raster, and pins the raster exactly where nothing moves) - which is deliberate: the grip is shorter than that label's line box, so the handle, the composer, and every shot other than the two with an open composer are unchanged. | CMH-SEL-03 | The `Add Comment` popup anchors to the last RENDERED character the selection covers, not to the last rect of the raw range. | CMH-CONTENT-IO-01 | `tools/authoring/content_extract.py` prints ONLY the fragment between the CONTENT markers, so an agent reads the 0.1 - 1.3 percent of a document it actually edits instead of a 1.4 - 2.5 MB file. The stored fragment is FINALIZED output (token spans, section cards, a baked TOC), so every code block that round-trips losslessly through the shared highlight inverse is handed back as plain SOURCE - the agent never hand-maintains span markup. De-highlighting is EMPIRICALLY verified, not assumed: a block is handed back as source only when re-highlighting that source reproduces the stored bytes AND the re-bake path would actually restore it. A block the inverse refuses (hand-written markup), one the re-bake does not touch (`language-text`, `language-kusto`, an unknown label), and one whose source contains a `<` next to a letter (`Array<string>`, `vector<int>`, `if x<y:` - which the re-bake skips as markup) are all passed through verbatim, so the loop never stalls and a raw angle bracket can never leak into the document. The region is anchored on the unique CONTENT markers exactly as `new_document.py` anchors it, so a decoy `<main id="commentRoot">` inside an authoring documentation comment is ignored. Formerly `CMH-CONTENT-01` (renamed in issue #904: the visual-content row of that id owned it first, and one feature id owns exactly one spec row). | `tests/test_content_io.py` - `ExtractTests` (`test_extract_returns_only_the_content_region`, `test_extract_is_a_small_fraction_of_the_document`, `test_extract_hands_back_de_highlighted_source`, `test_extract_ignores_a_decoy_content_root`); source: `tools/authoring/content_extract.py` - `extract()`, `content_span()`, `dehighlight_blocks()` |
| CMH-CONTENT-IO-02 | `tools/authoring/content_replace.py` writes a fragment back as ONE atomic transaction: it structurally checks the fragment, swaps the region, re-bakes (typography, section cards, highlighting, and an existing TOC), strict-validates, and re-stamps the content-bound validated hash. Either every step succeeds or the original file is left byte-for-byte unchanged with no temporary file surviving - the work file is removed from a `finally`, so a `KeyboardInterrupt` mid-transaction cannot leave a full copy of the user's document beside it either - there is no intermediate state an agent can wander away from, and no follow-up step it must remember. A replacement that produces no real change (compared ignoring the moving validated TIMESTAMP) does not touch the file at all, so rewriting a document with its own content is a true no-op rather than a fresh timestamp and a needless diff. Optionally marks Copy-all bundle ids handled in the same transaction, re-stamping afterwards. Formerly `CMH-CONTENT-02` (renamed in issue #904: the visual-content row of that id owned it first, and one feature id owns exactly one spec row). | `tests/test_content_io.py` - `ReplaceAtomicityTests` (`test_no_op_round_trip_is_byte_identical`, `test_edited_content_lands_and_is_re_highlighted`, `test_replace_re_stamps_the_validated_hash`, `test_a_failing_fragment_leaves_the_document_untouched`, `test_a_failing_fragment_leaves_no_temp_files_behind`, `test_replace_preserves_handled_ids_and_embedded_comments`, `test_cli_round_trip`); `tests/test_atomic_document_writes.py` - `StagedWorkFileTests`; source: `tools/authoring/content_replace.py` - `replace()`, `finalize_document()`, `splice()` |
| CMH-CONTENT-IO-03 | A content edit is LOCAL: a section the agent did not touch comes out of the round trip with a byte-identical hash, so its Mark-reviewed marker survives, while an edited section hashes differently. Byte fidelity is preserved too: before finalizing, every block whose SOURCE is unchanged has its ORIGINAL stored markup restored, so a document baked by an older tokenizer is not rewritten wholesale because one paragraph changed. A block whose markup the inverse refuses is reported to the caller rather than passed through silently, so the agent can tell clean source from markup it must edit by hand. (Section hashes are textContent-based, so re-baking never moves an untouched section's hash. The one documented exception is a legacy document that never went through finalize: re-baking normalizes its typography once, which is pinned by test rather than left as a surprise.) Entity-bearing prose (`&amp;`) survives unchanged, and a code block carrying hand-written markup is never rewritten. This is what stops a single paragraph edit from invalidating every review marker in the document or churning bytes in blocks whose highlighting predates the current tokenizer. Formerly `CMH-CONTENT-03` (renamed in issue #904: the visual-content row of that id owned it first, and one feature id owns exactly one spec row). | `tests/test_content_io.py` - `FidelityTests` (`test_untouched_sections_keep_identical_hashes`, `test_hand_written_markup_in_a_code_block_is_passed_through_verbatim`, `test_entity_bearing_prose_survives_the_round_trip`, `test_a_code_block_with_a_bare_less_than_round_trips`, `test_a_non_rehighlightable_block_is_never_de_escaped`, `test_a_kusto_block_is_left_escaped`, `test_generics_and_tight_comparisons_never_leak_a_raw_angle_bracket`, `test_an_unnormalized_legacy_section_is_normalized_on_first_replace`, `test_a_document_without_a_toc_does_not_gain_one`, `test_prose_mentioning_the_tool_is_not_mistaken_for_infrastructure`, `test_a_refused_block_is_reported_to_the_caller`, `test_an_older_tokenizers_markup_survives_an_unrelated_edit`) |
| CMH-CONTENT-IO-04 | `tools/authoring/extract_comments.py` prints the EMBEDDED comment snapshot as JSON (or as fenced text), serving the peer-review path where a returned Shareable file carries comments nobody pasted. It reports what is baked into the file, never "all current comments" - a reviewer's newer edits can still sit in browser `localStorage`, which no command-line tool can read. `--unhandled-only` drops ids already in `handledCommentIds`; malformed state is reported rather than guessed; and the text rendering wraps every reviewer note in a BEGIN/END UNTRUSTED REVIEWER NOTE fence so a downstream agent treats it as a document-scoped edit request, never as an instruction. ALL reviewer-controlled fields (the quote and author name as much as the note body) sit INSIDE the fence, since only the generated heading is trustworthy. The fence is defused, not merely wrapped: a note body (or metadata field) carrying the delimiter itself would otherwise close the fence early and make the rest read as trusted instructions. Formerly `CMH-CONTENT-04` (renamed in issue #904: the visual-content row of that id owned it first, and one feature id owns exactly one spec row). | `tests/test_content_io.py` - `CommentExtractionTests` (`test_extracts_the_embedded_snapshot`, `test_empty_state_is_an_empty_list_not_an_error`, `test_unhandled_only_drops_already_handled_ids`, `test_reviewer_text_is_fenced_as_untrusted`, `test_a_note_cannot_break_out_of_its_own_fence`, `test_all_reviewer_controlled_fields_are_inside_the_fence`, `test_malformed_state_is_reported_not_guessed`); source: `tools/authoring/extract_comments.py` - `extract_comments()`, `render_text()` |

Without this pin, a report/deck/theme whose ambient `line-height` is the keyword `normal` - or a direct `code { line-height: normal }` theme reset on the very `<code>` the gutter measures - would leave the computed value `"normal"`, `ensureCodeLineGutter()` would `parseFloat` it to `NaN` and fall back to a hardcoded `20px`, and the gutter numbers would sit above the text and drift down a tall block. | CMH-MMD-12 | After a REPORT diagram renders, the runtime VERIFIES what mermaid actually drew instead of laying the result out unconditionally, and repairs a bad render. Two invariants are measured: (1) LABEL FIT - every label's laid-out box fits the box that was sized for it, in SVG user units: an HTML label's `getBoundingClientRect` divided by the SVG's `getScreenCTM` scale (so a CSS-scaled diagram is judged in its own design units) against its `<foreignObject>` box, AND an SVG `<text>` label against its `g.node` shape, which is what keeps the post-repair comparison honest since an `htmlLabels:false` render has no `<foreignObject>` at all. The SVG-`<text>` arm is deliberately NARROW - only a `g.node` owning both a direct-child shape and mermaid's direct-child `g.label` wrapper is measured, so families that lay text against a composite or path-backed shape (class, requirement) or place free text with no owning shape (sequence, gantt, pie) are left unmeasured rather than risking a false positive that would re-render a healthy diagram. The measure reports the BOX COUNT alongside the worst overflow, because a worst of 0 means either "everything fits" or "nothing was measurable" and only the caller can tell those apart. The slack is `MMD_LABEL_SLACK` 4 user units; a healthy render overflows by exactly 0. (2) BOUNDS FIDELITY - the drawn content (`svg.getBBox()`, INTERSECTED with the `viewBox` so content drawn off to one side is judged by what actually lands inside it, plus `MMD_FILL_PAD` 24 units for mermaid's own 8-unit inset) fills at least `MMD_FILL_MIN` 0.7 of the `viewBox`. Only an UNDER-fill in BOTH axes counts as broken, because over-filling is normal (a gantt draws grid lines past its viewBox) and one small axis is a legitimate aspect ratio; the worst healthy fill across the shipped examples is 0.88, and the reported failure sat near 0.5 in both. A diagram failing either invariant is REPAIRED ONCE through the loader's `window.__cmhMermaidRerender` hook: the ONE failing host is re-rendered with `htmlLabels: false` (the deck-proven path, CMH-MMD-08 - SVG `<text>` labels scale with the diagram and cannot re-flow) on an off-screen clone of a PRISTINE pre-render DOM snapshot of the element (mermaid reads a diagram from `innerHTML` and normalizes `<br/>` in a node label, so re-rendering from serialized `textContent` would drop the authored line breaks and draw a DIFFERENT diagram), so the live element is replaced only once a good SVG exists and the document's default label mode is restored afterwards. `refitMermaidViewBox` then re-fits the bounds: SHRINK-ONLY and clamped to the content that lands INSIDE the current `viewBox`, since the fault being repaired is "the box is bigger than the drawing" - a rewrite that would ENLARGE the box (which a diagram drawing far outside its viewBox would otherwise produce, shrinking it to a speck) is refused outright - and it also re-derives mermaid's stale presentation size (the inline `max-width`, or the literal px `width`/`height` attributes an author's `useMaxWidth:false` produces, matched as lengths so a responsive `width="100%"` is left alone), rolling its own rewrite back unless the re-measured render improved. The repair is BOUNDED and never leaves a diagram worse: one attempt per host for the session (`host._cmhMmdRepairTried`), and the original SVG is kept aside and PUT BACK unless the re-render is no worse on every measured axis AND actually achieved something - a re-render that comes back just as broken, or one whose labels could not be measured at all and whose fill did not strictly improve, is rolled back rather than counted. A hook that cannot act (no snapshot, or a failed render) degrades to the same in-place bounds re-fit the no-hook path uses. Afterwards the comment rings are re-applied and `updateMermaidWidthClass` re-runs so the narrow/wide decision uses the corrected intrinsic width. Because the fault is SCALE-dependent, the automatic call sites re-measure a host when its rendered scale moves by more than `MMD_RESCALE_MIN` 5 percent (a resize, rotation, or reveal that changes the column), and a host whose one attempt is spent is never re-measured again; a diagram with no layout box (a collapsed section) is unmeasurable and is audited by the reveal `ResizeObserver` instead; a deck is excluded (it already renders SVG `<text>` labels and owns its contain-fit sizing). The same pristine snapshot and re-render hook are mirrored into the Export Offline vendored re-init - pinned against silent drift by a STRUCTURAL mirror test that normalizes both hook bodies and compares them, not just a spelling check - so an exported document keeps the protection. For automation, `window.__cmhMermaidAuditsSettled` is the verified-state gate: each host's audit slot is reserved SYNCHRONOUSLY the moment its render is observed, before the deferred measurement runs, so `await __cmhMermaidReady` then `await __cmhMermaidAuditsSettled` genuinely covers the verification; awaiting the render promise alone does not, because a repair is queued after it settles (both loaders do re-publish `window.__cmhMermaidReady` when a repair is queued, which helps a consumer that re-reads the global, but the settled-audits promise is the contract). `window.__cmhMermaidRepairs` (applied-repair count) and `window.__cmhMermaidAudit(host)` complete the automation surface. | CMH-LINK-01 | At render time, every author-facing `<a href>` document reference in `#commentRoot` is stamped `target="_blank"` so it opens in a new tab; links are classified by their normalized protocol (only `http`/`https`/`file`), so same-page `#` fragments, `.cm-skip` UI chrome, and non-document schemes (`javascript:`, `mailto:`, `tel:`, `data:`, including control-char-obfuscated variants) are never stamped or made commentable. When the URL parser cannot RESOLVE the href against this document there is no normalized protocol to read - `new URL()` throws - and the fallback is the CMH-LINK-05 gate's own string reading (`_cmhHrefIsDocumentReference`: the parser's inner tab/LF/CR strip and the shared `_cmhUrlEndsTrim` end trim, then the anchored scheme regex against `http`/`https`/`file`, with a scheme-less reference counting because it inherits the document's protocol), pinned to the validator's `_is_document_reference` as TEXT (all three character classes and the scheme set) and over a corpus. That is TWO populations, not one: an href the parser REJECTS outright (`http://[`, `http://%`, `file://[`, `https://?`), and ANY relative reference in a document whose base URL has an opaque path (`about:blank`, `blob:`, `data:`), which has no base to resolve against - so the everyday relative links of such a document are classified by this reading too. Reading `a.protocol` there was the defect: the HTML getter answers `":"` for an anchor whose URL record is null, which matches none of the three schemes, so such a link was left unstamped, an author-set `target="_self"` on it stood and navigated the reviewer's own tab away from the report and their comments, and the gate warned about a same-tab link the runtime never actually protected (#1183). The fallback can only ever ADD a stamp, since the branch it replaced answered false for every href that reached it. An author-set `target` on a document reference (`_self`/`_top`/a named frame) is OVERRIDDEN to `_blank` (opening a document reference in the same tab would strand the reviewer away from the report and their comments), while a non-document link keeps its author-set target; and `rel="noopener noreferrer"` is enforced (case-insensitively, decoupled from commentability) on ANY author link whose EFFECTIVE target is `_blank`. Effective, not raw: the operand is HTML's "get an element's target" - an anchor with no `target` of its own inherits the document's FIRST `<base target>`, and a name carrying BOTH an ASCII tab-or-newline and a U+003C is coerced to `_blank` (both characters are required; `x<` alone stays an ordinary name) - read through ONE shared reading (`_cmhEffectiveTarget` / `_CMH_TARGET_COERCE_WS_RE`, pinned as TEXT and over a corpus to the validator's `effective_link_target`, which CMH-KQL-05 and CMH-LINK-05 both use), so the readers cannot disagree about which links open a new tab. That `<base>` is the one a BROWSER applies: the lookup is namespace-filtered to an HTML `<base>` and never sees one parked in an inert `<template>` or a declarative shadow root, because a bare CSS type selector matches ANY namespace and an `<svg><base target="_self">` written before the real `<base target="_blank">` therefore masked it and silently lost the stamp (measured in Chromium). Only an HTML anchor INHERITS - HTML's rule is defined for an HTML `a`/`area`/`form` - so a foreign (SVG/MathML) `<a>`, which mermaid emits for a clickable node, is left alone rather than given a `noreferrer` that would suppress the Referer on a same-tab navigation. Reading the raw attribute left the whole NON-commentable set uncovered - a `#fragment`, a `mailto:`/`tel:` link - because those are never given a `target` of their own, so in a `<base target="_blank">` document they opened an auxiliary context with a live `window.opener` and nothing was stamped. The href that decides commentability is read the way the URL PARSER reads a URL: its ENDS are trimmed of C0 controls and space (U+0000-U+0020) through `_cmhUrlEndsTrim`, the JS twin of the validator's `url_ends_trim` (CMH-LINK-05), not with JS `.trim()`. Both the EMPTINESS test and the leading-`#` test move with it, since both decide the EARLY RETURN - so an over-broad trim makes the stamp apply to FEWER links, which is why this one is NOT the deliberately broader JS trim the `_blank` keyword match below keeps. The two trims differ in BOTH directions. JS `.trim()` removes NBSP, U+2028, U+2029, every Zs and U+FEFF, which the parser KEEPS, so `<a href="&#xa0;#frag" target="_self">` read as a same-page fragment and returned early, while a browser resolves it to a DIFFERENT document (`%C2%A0#frag`) and the author's `_self` therefore stood and navigated the reviewer's own tab away from the report and their comments; an NBSP-only `href="&#xa0;"` went the same way through the emptiness half (#1170). In the other direction JS `.trim()` KEEPS a non-whitespace C0 control that the parser removes, so `href="&#x1;#frag"` was read as a document reference although a browser navigates it inside this document. (U+0085 is kept by BOTH readings, so it is not part of the difference; the ASCII tab, VT and space both remove.) The same predicate gates link INDEXING, so every correction moves commentability with the stamp: a padded fragment is now commentable and a C0-padded one is not. The exemption the two string tests gate is then confirmed against the URL a browser RESOLVES (`_cmhSamePageHref`: the anchor's `href` property against `location.href`, both without their fragment), because a `<base href>` re-points BOTH an empty href and a bare `#fragment` at a DIFFERENT document - which a click then navigates the current tab to, the exact harm this row exists to prevent - so the string shape alone cannot decide it. The two guards are independent and both are load-bearing: the trim is what stops a parser-kept padding from reaching the resolved test at all and what lets a C0 padding reach it, while the resolved test is what stops a `<base href>` buying an exemption from a real cross-document navigation. The keyword match itself stays the JS `.trim().toLowerCase()`, deliberately BROADER than HTML's untrimmed ASCII-case-insensitive one: HTML reads a padded ` _blank` as a NAME, and a name this document does not declare opens a brand-new auxiliary context anyway, so tightening the match to the letter of the spec would REMOVE a stamp those links need. The stamp stays on the `_blank` KEYWORD rather than the gate's broader "opens an auxiliary browsing context": the gate only WARNS, while this MUTATES the document, and adding `noopener` to a link the author targeted by NAME would stop it reusing the context it named. The authored `rel` list is read the way HTML tokenizes one - on ASCII whitespace ONLY, through the bundle's single reading (`_offlineLinkRelTokens`, pinned to the validator's `link_rel_tokens`) - so a separator a browser does not tokenize on cannot fake a relation: a JS `\s` split also takes the vertical tab, NBSP and U+FEFF, so `rel="noopener<VT>x"` looked like it already named `noopener` and nothing was stamped, while the browser read ONE opaque relation, honored neither, and left `window.opener` exposed. The stored side is never re-normalized and the exact reading always wins: both readings are lossy in OPPOSITE directions (the current one empties the paddings the old one kept, the old one empties the paddings the current one keeps), so a single normalized compare would move a pre-1.790.0 comment on `href="&#x1;#frag"` onto a `href="&#x9;#frag"` link. `indexLinks` also CLEARS `cm-link-commentable` and `data-cm-link-index` from a link it does not index, because a document saved or exported by an older runtime carries the marks IT stamped and `findLinkEl` falls back to `[data-cm-link-index]`, so a stale attribute would resolve a comment onto a link this runtime does not consider commentable. The resolution order is by KEY STRENGTH within each href reading (the current one first, the pre-1.790.0 one only as a fallback): the link matching href + text, then the indexed candidate if its href matches, then the first href match. The stored `linkText` (`_cmhLinkTextKey`, the same collapse `linkInfo` stores) is what disambiguates links the href cannot tell apart: when two references share one href, an index that has gone stale by one lands on the WRONG one of them and the href test still passes, so the heal never ran and the comment silently re-anchored. Text therefore BEATS the index when the two disagree - a deliberate trade, since the index is the most fragile key the record holds (any change to which links are commentable shifts every later one). Its mirror case is indistinguishable from the same stored fields and is accepted: if a link's own label is edited AND a same-href sibling happens to carry the label it used to have, the comment follows the text onto that sibling (both links carried the same href AND text when the comment was written, so the record could not name one of them even then). A link whose label was edited with no same-href twin still heals by href alone, and two links sharing BOTH keys stay indistinguishable, with the index still deciding. | CMH-ANCHOR-01 | The structural-anchor layers (image, mermaid, diff, link, widget, heading) each own a floating `Add Comment` button but share ONE active-affordance sentinel: every layer reveals its button through `setActiveAdd()`, which hides and clears whichever OTHER layer's button was showing, so overlapping targets never leave two buttons up at once (single active affordance at a time). For a NESTED target - the common clickable-thumbnail/logo `<a><img></a>`, where the image layer's `<img>` lives inside the link layer's `<a>` and hovering fires both - the INNERMOST element owns the affordance (the image wins over the wrapping link), deterministically and independent of hover-event order, so the reader sees exactly one button; the image's own commenting (ring, card, reload) is unaffected. The same rule holds for any cross-layer overlap (for example a link inside a heading -> the inner link wins). For a non-nested (sibling) overlap where neither target contains the other, the last affordance shown wins. The innermost-wins tie-break only defers to an inner affordance that is STILL SHOWING: each layer's hide timer clears the shared sentinel via `clearActiveAdd()` when it hides its own button, so a dismissed inner affordance never keeps suppressing the enclosing layer (hovering the enclosing target afterward re-shows its button). ## Layered checklist

A `data-cmh-checklist` container is a hierarchical checklist. Any descendant carrying `data-cmh-state` or `data-cmh-item` is an item; an item with child items (nested lists, or table rows that name a parent via `data-cmh-parent`) is a branch that aggregates over its DIRECT children, otherwise a leaf. Leaf state cycles `blank -> check -> cross -> question -> blank`; a branch click propagates its next state to every descendant leaf. Only leaves whose state differs from their authored `data-cmh-state` baseline are stored, as one-character codes under `COMMENT_KEY + "::cl"`. Changes surface as one per-list card (jump + reset) placed by document order, a Copy-all section with `CHECKLIST_STATE_JSON`, and an export bake into `data-cmh-state`. Item identity is `data-cmh-item` when present, else the 1-based document-order position within the checklist; identity is never rendered (no visible numeration), so a checklist can live in a sortable table.

## Editable notes fields

A `data-cmh-note="<id>"` element is a single editable free-text field. The runtime replaces its
authored text with a `<textarea>` (with a single/multi-line toggle) whose baseline is the authored,
canonically-normalized `textContent`. Only a note whose current text differs from baseline is stored,
as `{id:text}` under `COMMENT_KEY + "::note"`; edits surface as one per-note change card (jump + reset)
placed by document order, a Copy-all section with `NOTES_STATE_JSON`, and an export bake into the
element's text. The field is `cm-skip` (editing never creates a highlight) and is set up before offset
restoration so its excluded text does not shift comment offsets. The one canonical normalizer (LF line
endings, trimmed outer whitespace) is implemented identically in the runtime and in
`tools/notes/notes_apply.py` so the browser and the cementing tool agree.

| Feature | Behavior | Test |
| --- | --- | --- |
| CMH-NOTE-01 | An authored `data-cmh-note` element upgrades to an editable `<textarea>`; the container gets `cm-skip` and `cmh-note-ready`, seeded with the authored text, alongside a label chip and a single/multi-line toggle. | `tests/62-notes.spec.js` - `CMH-NOTE-01: authored note upgrades to an editable textarea (cm-skip, ready, toggle)` |
| CMH-NOTE-02 | An edit stores a minimal delta (only when the normalized text differs from baseline) under `::note`; it restores on reload, and editing back to the exact baseline prunes the entry. | `tests/62-notes.spec.js` - `CMH-NOTE-02: an edit persists a minimal delta, restores on reload, and prunes at baseline` |

| CMH-NOTE-14 | `tools/notes/notes_scaffold.py` emits validator-clean `data-cmh-note` markup with a stable id, an optional label, escaped text, an optional multi-line default, and an optional foldable flag. | `tests/test_notes_scaffold.py` - `NotesScaffoldTests` |
| CMH-NOTE-15 | `validate.py` flags notes authoring mistakes as strict-escalated warnings (duplicate id, empty id, a nested note, a void-element note, a note with child elements, a note inside a checklist/diff/widget substrate), and is a no-op for a notes-free document. A note anywhere on a deck slide (or `.deck-stage`) is NOT flagged - live notes on a slide are a supported pattern (used by the showcase deck, where the notes sit inside slide layout wrappers) - because a slide, unlike a checklist/diff/widget, does not mark its descendant text `cm-skip`; a note nested inside a checklist/diff/widget that sits on a slide is still flagged. | `tests/test_notes_validate.py` - `NotesValidateTests` |
| CMH-NOTE-16 | A `data-cmh-note-foldable` note is a disclosure: a `+`/`-` toggle on the header line reveals or hides the field on the line below. It starts collapsed only when empty (a note with content, authored or a persisted edit, starts expanded); the fold state is session-only, evaluated once at load, so a manual collapse sticks. The toggle is an accessible `<button>` (`aria-expanded`, `aria-controls`), a collapsed note that still holds content is badged, `jumpToNote` expands a collapsed note before focusing it, and the collapse never reaches storage or the exported source. The disclosure is keyed off RUNTIME-owned classes only (`cmh-note-ready` compounded with the state class), so it works for any element carrying `data-cmh-note` regardless of its author-supplied class list (`class="cmh-note"` is cosmetic card chrome, never load-bearing) while keeping its selector strength; a runtime state class found in the AUTHORED markup is cleared at load, so a note can never be authored into a state its own controls cannot undo. Hovering the fold button is a real cue - the fill changes - and the `+`/`-` glyph stays legible on that fill (at least 4.5:1 in both the light and dark themes), never repainted in the same token as the fill; author CSS that restyles `.cmh-note-fold` at higher specificity still wins, as any author override does. A note collapsed on screen is revealed for print. | `tests/62-notes.spec.js` - `CMH-NOTE-16: a foldable note starts collapsed only when empty and toggles with the +/- control`, `CMH-NOTE-16: keyboard toggles the fold, and a collapsed note with content shows a badge`, `CMH-NOTE-16: a foldable note with a persisted edit auto-expands on reload; jump expands a collapsed note`, `CMH-NOTE-16: fold state is presentation only - the export keeps data-cmh-note-foldable but no runtime collapse`, `CMH-NOTE-16: hide collapses a foldable note carrying no author cmh-note class`, `CMH-NOTE-16: an authored runtime state class is cleared, so the field is never stuck hidden`, `CMH-NOTE-16: the fold button keeps its +/- glyph legible on hover`, `CMH-NOTE-16: print reveals a collapsed class-less note` |
| CMH-NOTE-17 | Typing in a note field coalesces the sidebar re-render: because `renderComments()` runs full-document text-node and section scans, a burst of keystrokes schedules a single debounced render (a note's document position does not move while its text is edited) instead of one scan per keystroke, so typing does not freeze a large document. The edit is persisted synchronously on every keystroke and the lightweight UI (shareability badge, Copy-all affordance, first-change sidebar auto-open when Auto-open panel on comment is on) updates synchronously on the dirty-state transition (never per keystroke, so a burst does no per-key document scan), so an export or Copy all fired mid-burst reflects the latest text; only the sidebar-list card is deferred, rendering once the reviewer pauses. Programmatic reset / clear-all still render immediately. | `tests/62-notes.spec.js` - `CMH-NOTE-17: typing coalesces the sidebar re-render (one debounced render per burst, not one per keystroke)`, `CMH-NOTE-17: a Copy all during the debounce window reflects the latest text and the badge updates synchronously` |

| CMH-COPY-08 | Copy all treats reviewer notes, document text, the document label, and the document source as untrusted: it strips Unicode bidi/format controls (`U+202A-U+202E`, `U+2066-U+2069`, `U+200E/U+200F`) from human-readable payload text, and escapes those controls in machine-readable JSON identifiers so apply tools still parse the original ids without raw invisible controls in the bundle. Each free-text note is otherwise wrapped in a dynamic, tilde-sized `UNTRUSTED REVIEWER NOTE` fence (longer than any tilde run in the note), a read-first AGENT INSTRUCTIONS block frames notes as document-scoped change requests (data, not agent/system instructions), and `data-doc-source` is emitted single-line with backticks neutralized so an embedded newline cannot forge a standalone machine line and a backtick cannot close the Markdown code span it sits in. | `tests/05-copy-handled.spec.js` - `forged trailer/instruction lines in a note or doc-source are neutralized (CMH-COPY-08/09)`; `tests/05-copy-handled.spec.js` - `bidi formatting controls in notes, document text, and metadata are stripped from Copy all (CMH-COPY-08)`; `tests/05-copy-handled.spec.js` - `the untrusted-note fence tilde run outgrows a long tilde run in the note (CMH-COPY-08)`; `tests/12-features.spec.js` - `the bundle carries the full documented contract for a text comment` |
| CMH-COPY-09 | All machine-readable JSON (`HANDLED_IDS_JSON`, `NOTES_STATE_JSON`, `CHECKLIST_STATE_JSON`) is emitted only inside ONE unconditional final `=== CMH MACHINE TRAILER (do not edit) ===` block (canonical empty values when there are no changes); the three Python apply tools read JSON only from within that fenced trailer (last open marker) and FAIL CLOSED when the opening marker has no matching END marker, so a forged trailer/state line in a note body or doc-source is ignored. | `tests/05-copy-handled.spec.js` - `forged trailer/instruction lines in a note or doc-source are neutralized (CMH-COPY-08/09)`; `tests/test_notes_apply.py` - `test_from_bundle_reads_only_the_machine_trailer`, `test_from_bundle_ignores_forged_line_when_no_changes`, `test_from_bundle_fails_closed_on_unclosed_trailer`; `tests/test_checklist_apply.py` - `test_from_bundle_ignores_forged_line_outside_trailer`, `test_from_bundle_ignores_forged_line_when_no_changes`, `test_from_bundle_fails_closed_on_unclosed_trailer`; `tests/test_mark_handled.py` - `test_bundle_parsing_uses_last_authoritative_contract`, `test_bundle_parsing_fails_closed_on_unclosed_trailer` |
| CMH-HANDLED-01 | The agent treats the `HANDLED_IDS_JSON` line inside the final `=== CMH MACHINE TRAILER (do not edit) ===` block as the machine-readable contract and appends those ids to `<script id="handledCommentIds">`; a forged `HANDLED_IDS_JSON` line elsewhere in the bundle is ignored. | `tests/test_mark_handled.py` - `test_bundle_parsing`, `test_bundle_parsing_uses_last_authoritative_contract`, `test_cli_from_bundle_stdin` |
| CMH-HANDLED-02 | On load, ids in `handledCommentIds` are pruned from memory and `localStorage`, and matching highlights or rings disappear. | `tests/05-copy-handled.spec.js` - `marking an id handled prunes it on reload and from Copy all (via mark_handled.py)`; `tests/04-comments-code-mermaid.spec.js` - `a mermaid comment prunes on reload once marked handled` |
| CMH-HANDLED-03 | Copy all filters handled comments even if storage still contains them, so handled ids never reappear in the bundle or count. | `tests/05-copy-handled.spec.js` - `marking an id handled prunes it on reload and from Copy all (via mark_handled.py)`; `tests/12-features.spec.js` - `a handled mermaid comment is excluded from Copy all after reload` |
| CMH-HANDLED-04 | `mark_handled.py` edits only the handled-id JSON block, dedupes ids, validates id shape, preserves order and newline style, and refuses ambiguous duplicate blocks. | `tests/test_mark_handled.py` - `test_only_the_block_changes`, `test_dedupes_and_preserves_order`, `test_rejects_unsafe_id_without_writing`, `test_preserves_crlf`, `test_rejects_multiple_real_blocks`, `test_cli_appends_and_is_idempotent` |

## Export security invariants

| Feature id | Behavior | Covering tests |
| --- | --- | --- |
| CMH-EXP-14 | The whole-document `DOMParser -> doc.documentElement.outerHTML` round-trip used in the export/apply paths (`36-checklist.js`, `37-notes.js`, `65-export-shareable.js`, `66-export-plain.js`, `67-export-standalone.js`, `68-export-offline.js`, `84-section-review.js`) is safe only because comment/state data never enters it as markup and host HTML is a trusted, unsanitized boundary (CMH-SEC-01). Every `parseFromString()` call site feeds only the trusted document `html` string, never a comment `note`, `quote`, `author`, or any other user-supplied field. The two DERIVED strings are held to the same rule by construction: `srcProbed` (65-export-shareable.js) splices a fixed probe attribute into walked `<script>` open tags, and `stamped` (67-export-standalone.js, CMH-EXP-22) replaces each located region marker with a fixed alphanumeric probe token - neither admits document content, let alone comment data. If host-HTML sanitization is ever added upstream, this round-trip must be re-audited for serialization-differential stored XSS before landing. | `tests/test_export_domparser_guard.py` - `test_domparser_call_sites_never_take_comment_fields`, `test_domparser_call_sites_use_the_trusted_html_variable`, `test_domparser_present_only_in_expected_partials`; source: `assets/js/36-checklist.js` - `_applyChecklistStateToHtml()`, `assets/js/37-notes.js` - `_applyNoteStateToHtml()`, `assets/js/65-export-shareable.js` - `_applyWidgetLayoutToHtml()`, `assets/js/68-export-offline.js` - `_offlineDocFromHtml()` |
| CMH-EXP-16 | The embedded-comments block and the layer descriptor beside it are resolved as INFRASTRUCTURE, never by scanning document text: a tag walk that follows the HTML tokenizer (it consumes comments - including the empty `<!-->` form and a `--!>` terminator - DOCTYPEs, bogus declarations and processing instructions; skips the TEXT content of raw-text elements, ends one only on an exact end tag, and follows the script-data escaped and double-escaped states behind the `<!--<script>` idiom; treats `<template>` content as the inert fragment `getElementById` cannot see, nesting included; and tokenizes tag names and attributes on ASCII whitespace only) finds the `<script>` whose PARSED `id` matches, and the result is CROSS-CHECKED against the browser's own parse of the same source before anything is spliced by offsets. Resolution requires the walk and the parsed document to AGREE on how many scripts own the id - and the block a reader resolves must be one of those scripts - so a non-script element shadowing the id, or any walk/parser disagreement, resolves to nothing instead of being spliced on a guess; WHICH of several owners is the layer's own block is decided by the content-root boundary (CMH-EXP-17), never by document position. The layer's own source is part of every document and necessarily spells that markup, so a text scan was answered by the runtime itself - the "make sure the EMBEDDED COMMENTS region is present" guard could never fire, a document that had genuinely lost the region silently exported a copy whose runtime source had been overwritten mid-function with the comments JSON, and the same defect in the descriptor path overwrote a quarter of a megabyte of runtime on every Offline export of such a document. A document missing the block now fails loudly (Save, Shareable, Standalone, and Offline alike) and downloads nothing, with a distinct message for "region absent" and "present but could not be located reliably"; a mention that exists only inside content a browser parses as text never resolves; and `_getBaseHtml` accepts a fetched on-disk copy only when a real block resolves in it, falling back to the DOM snapshot otherwise. The LOAD-TIME snapshot is the one caller that cannot run the pass at capture time, because it must remain the FIRST statement in the IIFE (nothing may mutate the DOM before it, and `tests/test_assets_split.py` pins that) while the pass depends on `const`s that are not hoisted. So the capture takes the RAW assembly (`cmhSerializeElementRaw`) and the PURE transform is applied to it a few lines later, once those declarations exist - the same single rule, deferred rather than duplicated. DECLARED LIMIT: the walk keeps no namespace stack, so it reads FOREIGN content as it would the HTML namespace. Nothing is raw text inside `<svg>` / `<math>`, so an `<svg><style>` body IS escaped by the serializer and IS decoded by the parser but is left verbatim here; and an `<svg><plaintext>` is an ordinary foreign element that does NOT swallow the rest of the document, yet the walk stops rewriting after it. Both directions only DECLINE to improve fidelity - the opposite would corrupt a real script or style body into showing six literal characters - so the walk errs there on purpose. A `<script>` or `<style>` body in the HTML namespace loses a CR too, and irrecoverably: no character reference is decoded there, so there is no spelling that survives - which is also why a state bake that re-parses the assembled base (`_applyWidgetLayoutToHtml` and the checklist/notes/review appliers) folds one. Closing the foreign-content gap properly would mean modelling the HTML integration points (`<foreignObject>`, `<desc>`, SVG `<title>`, the MathML text points) and every breakout tag, and a half-correct stack lands on the CORRUPTING side, so declining beats guessing. Nothing here touches a CONTENT HASH: the document and section hashes read live DOM text (`CMH-CONTENT-21`, `CMH-REVIEW`), never the serialized string, so this pass cannot drift one - it makes them MORE stable, since a CR-bearing document previously came back from an export as an LF-bearing one and flipped its own validation banner. | `tests/97-export-cr-fidelity.spec.js` - `an attribute value keeps its CR through Export as Shareable (CMH-EXP-24)`, `a text node keeps its CR through Export as Shareable (CMH-EXP-24)`, `text and attribute values are rewritten (CMH-EXP-24)`, `a string with no CR is returned unchanged (CMH-EXP-24)`, `a script or style body is left verbatim while its start tag is rewritten (CMH-EXP-24)`, `a comment body is left verbatim (CMH-EXP-24)`, `RCDATA text is rewritten, because a browser decodes a reference there (CMH-EXP-24)`, `a less-than sign inside an attribute value does not open a raw-text region (CMH-EXP-24)`, `a plaintext element makes the rest of the document verbatim (CMH-EXP-24)`, `a script end tag that only prefixes the name does not end the body (CMH-EXP-24)`, `a text node after the layer script keeps its CR (CMH-EXP-24)`, `Export Offline keeps an attribute value's CR (CMH-EXP-24)`, `the double-escaped script-data idiom resolves the element close (CMH-EXP-24)`, `an unterminated tag or raw-text body leaves the remainder intact (CMH-EXP-24)`, `the pass only ever substitutes, never loses or reorders content (CMH-EXP-24)`, `a foreign plaintext declines the rewrite rather than risking a raw-text body (CMH-EXP-24)`, `the document-source rewrite keeps a CR in the value it re-encodes (CMH-EXP-24)`, `markup-shaped tail text stays text, so its CR still round-trips (CMH-EXP-24)`, `a foreign style body is left verbatim while later text is still rewritten (CMH-EXP-24)`, `a character-reference CR decodes to a CR, not an LF (CMH-EXP-24)`, `a literal newline and a leading newline are preserved (CMH-EXP-24)`, `ordinary references and markup characters decode unchanged (CMH-EXP-24)`; source: `assets/js/00-preamble.js` - `cmhEscapeSerializedCarriageReturns()`, `cmhEscapeCr()`, `cmhSerializeTextData()`, `cmhSerializeElement()`; `assets/js/65-export-shareable.js` - `_snapshotWithTail()`, `_cmhDecodeAttribute()`, `_cmhEncodeAttribute()` |

| CMH-PORT-04 | Migration is fail-safe on hostile or ambiguous input, because it rewrites the user's only copy of a document in place. (a) Companion bytes are inlined with any raw-text terminator for their host element escaped, so a `--dist` whose stylesheet carries `</StYlE><script>` cannot turn control of a stylesheet into script execution; the payload is neutralized, never silently dropped. (b) The write is staged in the target's directory and swapped in with `os.replace` (shared `_atomic_io.atomic_write`, which also follows a symlink to its target, gives the staged file the destination's `0777` permission bits so `mkstemp`'s `0600` cannot silently narrow a world-readable document - never copying setuid/setgid/sticky onto the staged inode, leaving the mode alone when an existing destination cannot be statted so a guess can never widen a private file, using the umask-derived default for a destination that does not exist yet (the transform CLIs pass their own source document to `preserve_mode` instead, so a new `--out` keeps the source's visibility - intersected with what a plain create would produce, so it is never wider than either the source or the umask allows), reporting a failed mode step on stderr rather than landing the wrong permissions silently, and clearing a read-only staged file so cleanup cannot leak it), so an interrupted or failing write leaves the original intact instead of truncating it to zero bytes - the staged file is cleaned up from a `finally`, so an interrupt mid-write cannot leak it either. The swap itself is retried on Windows, where `os.replace` fails with a sharing violation (`winerror` 32/33) while another process holds the destination open (a virus scanner, an editor, a sync client) and a truncating write would have succeeded; the retry is short and BOUNDED (four backed-off waits, ~0.75s), so a genuinely locked file still fails loudly and leaks no staged file, and any other `PermissionError` - a POSIX one, or a Windows access-denied, neither of which waiting can fix - is raised at once. The retry is shared as `_atomic_io.commit_staged` (mode preservation, the retried swap, and the directory fsync), so the tools that hand-roll their own staging (`upgrade.py`, `retrofit.py`, `deck/deck_theme.py`) make the same durable swap after flushing their staged bytes with `_atomic_io.fsync_file`. Every tool that rewrites a document shares this writer and therefore its residuals (CMH-TOOL-22): the result is a NEW inode, so ownership/ACLs and hard-link identity are not carried over, and on POSIX it is the DIRECTORY's write permission that permits the swap. (c) EVERY anchor - the CONTENT span, the bootstrap block, the loader note, each companion element and the descriptor - is resolved against the document's ORIGINAL bytes and applied as one pass of non-overlapping edits, so untrusted companion text can never aim a later step; and candidates are found in a view with HTML comments and raw-text bodies blanked, so a commented-out or quoted copy of an element is never the one rewritten. (d) Ambiguity is refused rather than guessed: a duplicated CONTENT marker, more than one live descriptor, or more than one live reference to the same companion aborts before anything is written, and a result that would still reference a companion outside CONTENT is refused too. (e) The mode transition parses the layer descriptor as JSON and requires exactly one nonshareable -> shareable transition, so a reformatted descriptor can no longer be reported as migrated while still marked nonshareable, and a document with no parsable descriptor is refused. | `tests/test_to_shareable.py` - `HostileLayerTests`, `SafeWriteTests`, `ContentMarkerIntegrityTests`, `DescriptorTests`, `LiveMarkupOnlyTests`, `AuthoredScaffoldingTests`; `tests/test_atomic_io.py` - `PreserveModeTests`, `ReplaceRetryTests`; `tests/48-to-shareable.spec.js` - `a migrated document opens, comments and copies like a native Shareable one (CMH-PORT-04)`, `a hostile dist cannot execute script in a migrated document (CMH-PORT-04)` |

| CMH-UI-13 | `Clear all comments` is reachable from the toolbar overflow menu (`#btnClearAllTop`) as well as the sidebar More menu (`#btnClearAll`), grouped immediately after `Manage storage` with the same label, trash icon, and `danger` styling, so a reviewer working with the comments panel hidden can clear without re-opening it. Both ids bind to ONE handler, so the confirmation text, the nothing-to-clear guard (no dialog, no state change), and the reset semantics (comments, notes, checklist, widget layout, open editors and popovers) are identical; only the focus-restore target differs, landing on the trigger of whichever menu the user opened (`#btnToolbarMenu` for the toolbar). A repeat activation while the confirmation is already up returns without moving focus, so the caret is never pulled out of the `aria-modal` dialog. The overflow menu closes on the action and its trigger's `aria-expanded` resets, leaving the Escape/focus contract of CMH-UI-10 unchanged, and the toolbar count pill and mode badge refresh afterwards. | `tests/32-ui-batch5.spec.js` - `the overflow menu groups Clear all comments beside Manage storage (CMH-UI-13)`, `clearing from the overflow menu works with the panel hidden (CMH-UI-13)`, `the overflow menu Clear all runs the same confirmed flow as the sidebar item (CMH-UI-13)`, `with nothing to clear both entry points are inert and keep focus on their trigger (CMH-UI-13)`, `a repeat activation while the confirm dialog is open does not pull focus out of it (CMH-UI-13)`; `tests/20-ui-chrome.spec.js` - `the overflow menu header brand mark links to the project site (CMH-MENU-ICON-02)` (its focus-order equality also pins that `#btnClearAllTop` is in the menu's tab order); source: `assets/template.shell.html`, `assets/js/62-sortable-tables.js`, `assets/css/30-mermaid.css` |
| CMH-UI-14 | A chrome control focused while its panel is still SLIDING IN gets its styled tooltip once the control lands, instead of losing it for good. The tip is only ever raised by `focusin`/`mouseover`, so a control that is momentarily outside the visible box during the 0.22s sidebar slide used to be suppressed with no second chance - a keyboard user who opened the panel and immediately tabbed to Search/Sort/More/Help got silence. A suppressed anchor now opens a bounded watch EPISODE (a single `requestAnimationFrame` loop, timed on a monotonic clock): the tip is raised the moment the anchor is inside the visible box, up to `CM_TIP_LAND_MS` (600ms, comfortably longer than the slide) later. Because an anchor counts as visible as soon as it overlaps the box by a pixel - long before a slide settles - the bubble then KEEPS following the control until its box holds still for two frames, so it ends up beside the settled control with its arrow on the control's centre rather than parked where the control was mid-animation; that follow runs for any shown tip, so a control already inside the box but still moving is tracked too. The rect is compared at half-pixel resolution, so subpixel jitter does not read as movement. Each frame reads visibility BEFORE the deadline, so a frame delayed past the budget (a backgrounded tab pauses `requestAnimationFrame`) still shows the tip for a control that did land. The suppression itself is unchanged for an anchor the reviewer genuinely cannot see (a soft keyboard covering it, a pinch-panned page): an episode requires the control to still be focused or hovered, is bounded as a WHOLE (one landing deadline plus an outer tracking deadline, so an animation that never settles cannot renew it), and ends when focus or the pointer moves on (taking any bubble already shown with it), on the usual dismissals (focus out, scroll, viewport change, Escape, mousedown), and when another anchor takes over - so it expires quietly rather than parking a bubble over unrelated chrome or popping one up over a control the reviewer has already tabbed past. | `tests/32-ui-batch5.spec.js` - `a control focused while the panel is still sliding in gets its tooltip once it lands (CMH-UI-14)`, `a control that never becomes visible gets no parked tooltip (CMH-UI-14)`, `focus moving on before the control lands cancels the pending tooltip (CMH-UI-14)`; source: `assets/js/95-startup.js` - `_cmTipTrack()`, `_cmTipLandTick()`, `_cmTipRectKey()`, `_cmTipOnScreen()` |

| CMH-SIDE-13 | Every rendered INSTANT names the timezone it is in, so two reviewers in different zones read the same comment the same way: the shared `formatTime()` appends the viewer's zone as the locale names it (`PST`, `GMT+3`), falling back to a computed `UTC+HH:MM` offset where the engine cannot part a zone name out. It is appended by the runtime rather than left to `timeZoneName`, so the separator (and, in UTC mode, the wording) is the same in every locale; the `Intl.DateTimeFormat` is built once PER FORMATTING PASS and reused for every timestamp in it - a render, a Copy all bundle, or a print appendix each start a fresh pass - which keeps the per-timestamp cost down without pinning a zone for the whole session (a constructed formatter fixes the zone it resolved, while `toLocaleString` keeps following the OS, so a session-long memo would name the old zone beside a clock already showing the new one after the reviewer travels). Because `formatTime()` is the single formatter, the label reaches every surface at once: comment cards and replies, the in-document comment dialog, the board-summary state cards, the sidebar `Generated on` / `Last comment` rows, the runtime footer, the Copy all bundle, and the print appendix. Its input contract is total over the shapes a store can hold: a nullish, empty, or whitespace-only value renders as EMPTY (never `undefined`, `Invalid Date`, or the Unix epoch `new Date(null)` would produce), an epoch-milliseconds NUMBER or a `Date` is accepted as the instant it is, a string is TRIMMED once so a padded ISO instant formats instead of being echoed raw, an otherwise unparseable value is handed back as its own trimmed text, and the return is always a string. Where a comment has no usable timestamp, the surrounding chrome goes with it: the card, reply, and dialog meta lines drop the separator rather than showing a dangling `#3 - `, and the Copy all bundle emits no `When:` line. The edit time wins on those meta lines only when it FORMATS, so an `updatedAt` that is present but unusable falls back to the creation time instead of hiding it or claiming `(edited)` with nothing to show. A DATE-ONLY value (`YYYY-MM-DD`) is a CALENDAR date, not an instant, so it keeps its bare no-time rendering (CMH-SIDE-03) and carries NO zone in EITHER display mode, which would imply a precision it does not have; its out-of-range `Date` rollover (`2026-02-30` reading as March 2) is the pre-existing CMH-SIDE-03 behavior and is deliberately unchanged. In UTC mode the label is only claimed where the engine really honors `toLocaleString`'s `timeZone` option (probed once at load against TWO instants six months apart, so a zone that merely happens to sit at `+00:00` on one of them cannot read as honored); an engine that drops the option gets the fixed-format UTC serialization instead, so local time is never printed under a `UTC` label. | `tests/99-timestamp-zone.spec.js` - `CMH-SIDE-13: a comment card timestamp names the local timezone`, `CMH-SIDE-13: the sidebar Generated-on row and the footer name the timezone`, `CMH-SIDE-13: replies and the print appendix carry the zone too`, `CMH-SIDE-13: a date-only generated value stays a bare calendar date with no zone`, `CMH-SIDE-13: a missing or padded timestamp formats sanely instead of leaking Invalid Date`, `CMH-SIDE-13: an engine that ignores the timeZone option never labels local time as UTC`, `CMH-SIDE-13: the zone formatter is built once per formatting pass, not once per timestamp`, `CMH-SIDE-13: an engine with no zone-name part falls back to a computed UTC offset`; source: `assets/js/50-sidebar.js` - `formatTime()`, `cmhFormatInstant()`, `cmhLocalZoneLabel()`, `cmhTimeMetaHtml()`, `CMH_TZ_OPTION_HONORED` |

A match on a parent narrows away its non-matching subsections (ancestors are kept, descendants are not). Escape (or clearing the box) restores the complete tree, and a deep link OR a comment/widget jump to a filtered-out entry reveals AND expands it instead of scrolling to nothing - testing for ANY filtered `<section>` ancestor, and for the entry's own hidden row when its wrapper stayed visible. The filter box hides when the menu is collapsed and clears when the viewport narrows below the menu breakpoint. Each entry is matched on its TITLE ALONE - the entry label, which is an author `.cm-toc` link's text or else the heading's own text - and never on the section's body prose, so a word that appears only in a paragraph no longer keeps that section (or its menu entry) listed. Query and title are compared case-insensitively after collapsing internal whitespace runs and trimming, so source line breaks and indentation inside a heading cannot decide a match. The title a query sees is what the menu SHOWS, minus the number the runtime itself computes: the row's resolved title plus the number the DOCUMENT supplies (the one `generate_toc` strips from the label into the `.cm-toc-num` span, CMH-TOC-10), so typing `10.3` finds the row that reads `10.3 Vendor exposure` exactly as it does when the author left the number in the label, and matches its `10.3.1` subsection the same substring way any other title text does. The sequential number the runtime COMPUTES for a document that supplies none is chrome rather than title text and never matches, and the review status mark is a CSS pseudo-element (CMH-REVIEW-11) so it cannot leak in either. The row and the filter resolve ONE title per entry, so a query can never surface a row whose title the reader cannot read: an author nav link with no text of its own (an icon-only link) falls back to the text of the heading it targets, minus a leading number the `.cm-toc-num` span already shows, and that same title is what the row renders. The fallback is resolved AFTER the numbering mode is chosen, so a heading-derived title can never flip the document to author-numbered or suppress another entry's number, and it is taken only for a heading target, so a nav link that points at a wrapper element never pulls that element's prose into a title. A document whose headings all share one wrapper `<section>` narrows like any other, since each entry carries its own title. A `<section>` that owns an entry is hidden only when EVERY entry inside it is filtered out (so a wrapper can never be hidden out from under a matching heading), the section lookup is scoped to the content root at BOTH ends - the target must be inside it and so must the `<section>` found for it, so a root that sits inside the host page's own section never marks host chrome - and a query that matches NOTHING narrows the menu only rather than blanking the document. Filtered sections use `display:none` (offset-safe) in SCREEN media only: print and Save as PDF force them back, so a reader's transient filter can never truncate a printed document. | CMH-TOC-12 | In a FLOW DOCUMENT (never a deck - the whole in-document navigation family, section collapse and the side menu included, is deliberately flow-only, so a deck slide's authored `.cm-toc` gets no caret and is left exactly as written, as plain content rather than half-folded), an in-document `.cm-toc` Contents list is COLLAPSIBLE: the runtime injects a caret into its title row that folds the list away and unfolds it, clicking a folded title unfolds it too (expand-only, and never mid-selection, so commenting on the title of an open list is unaffected), and the folded title row stays on screen so the block still says what it is and the control that brings the list back is reachable. The fold is READER state, not document state, and that is enforced three ways. The caret is a runtime-injected, TEXT-FREE `cm-skip` button (its glyph is a `::before`) registered as layer chrome, so it spends no character of the offset space comments are anchored in - the live `docHash()` still equals the SOURCE file's `document_content_hash`, folded or not. Folding only toggles a class; no node is removed or reordered, so a comment inside or below the list keeps its anchor. And the choice persists in a PER-DOCUMENT `localStorage` key (`COMMENT_KEY::tocFold`, registered in `CMH_SUBKEY_SUFFIXES` so the storage manager accounts for it as this document's data rather than as a phantom document - CMH-STORE-09). Each list is remembered under a STABLE identity - the nav's authored id (namespaced `id:`), else a SIGNATURE of the COMPLETE sequence of entry targets it lists (namespaced `sig:`, each href percent-encoded before joining so a separator inside one cannot forge a boundary, and the two namespaces disjoint so an authored id can never collide with a signature) - with two navs that resolve to the same identity (duplicate authored ids are legal HTML, and two lists can genuinely list the same entries) told apart by their order among themselves, so a document that later gains another Contents list above this one neither moves the reader's fold onto a different list nor lets a newcomer steal it - not one whose single entry repeats this list's first target, and not one that shares this list's first target, last target and count while listing different sections in between. Several lists in one document fold independently. The map is read through a guarded parse that treats absent, unparseable, or non-object storage as "nothing folded", is copied onto a NULL-PROTOTYPE object (the one convention this runtime has for a document-reachable state map, CMH-SEC-02), and counts only the exact `1` sentinel as folded, so neither a truthy-but-wrong stored value nor a key another script polluted onto `Object.prototype` can fold a list the reader never folded. A comment can be anchored ON a Contents entry, so the jump path unfolds EVERY folded list it sits in - walking nested `.cm-toc` ancestors to the outermost, the way `expandCollapsedAncestors()` walks nested sections, since opening only the inner one would leave the comment hidden inside a still-folded outer list - and it unfolds through the owning toggle, so the caret's aria state and the stored choice stay consistent. - without that the fold would be a third `display:none` mechanism `expandCollapsedAncestors()` does not know about, and a persisted fold would make the dead jump sticky. The caret's `aria-controls` names the NAV, not its first list, because the fold hides every child but the title row - and it names an id that RESOLVES to that nav: assistive technology follows `aria-controls` with `getElementById`, which answers with the first element carrying the id, so a nav whose AUTHORED id is duplicated elsewhere is given a minted runtime id (`cmhToc<n>`, chosen by probing the WHOLE document so it collides with nothing - an authored `id="cmhToc0"` is never taken from the nav that carries it) rather than left pointing at the other element's region. The trigger is "this id does not resolve to me", so it also fires when an unrelated EARLIER element (an `<a id="contents">` anchor target, say) shadows the nav, which is exactly the case where the caret would otherwise name a region it does not control. A nav whose id is unique is never re-identified. The declared trade-off: on that degenerate input - two elements sharing one id, which is invalid HTML - an author rule or script keyed to `#contents` stops matching the SHADOWED nav. That is accepted, because announcing the wrong region to a screen reader is a defect a reader cannot see or work around, while the id collision is authored and visible. The authored id still supplies the STORAGE identity, resolved before the mint, so re-identifying a nav for ARIA never orphans a reader's stored fold. The fold is a CSS rule over ELEMENT children, which cannot reach a text node, so a nav that carries significant text DIRECTLY (an intro sentence beside its list, or entries written as bare text) would otherwise fold half way - the caret saying the list is away while the sentence stays on screen. Each non-whitespace direct text run is therefore wrapped in a `span.cmh-toc-text` that the same rule hides, and that print restores with the rest. The wrapper is deliberately NOT `cm-skip`: the text is the author's, and dropping it out of the offset space would move every comment anchored below it; moving the same text node under a new inline parent leaves that space untouched. Every export builds from the on-disk source, so neither the caret node nor the fold class can bake into an exported document. Print and Save as PDF force the whole list back (screen-media fold only, mirroring `section.cm-toc-filtered`), while the caret itself stays hidden as chrome - including in the single-page print measurement, whose height must match what prints. The value is CROSS-DOCUMENT only, in `commentable-html::utcTimes`, and deliberately has no per-document override - the zone a reviewer reads in is a property of the reader, not of the document - so it persists across reload and applies to every commentable-html document in that browser. Every read and write is `try/catch` guarded, a refused write reports itself with the same Manage-storage toast rather than silently snapping the row back, the row re-syncs from storage on a cross-tab `storage` event, and the key is registered in the storage manager's shared-preferences list so it is billed to the shared bucket. | `tests/99-timestamp-zone.spec.js` - `CMH-MENU-PREF-10: the More menu carries a Show times in UTC row that toggles in place and persists`, `CMH-MENU-PREF-10: the UTC row is keyboard operable and re-syncs on a cross-tab change`, `CMH-MENU-PREF-10: a refused UTC-preference write reports itself instead of silently snapping back`; source: `assets/template.shell.html`, `assets/js/01-config.js`, `assets/js/06-preferences.js`, `assets/js/55-toolbar-menu.js`, `assets/js/57-storage-manager.js` |
| CMH-MENU-PREF-11 | With the preference ON, `formatTime()` normalizes the instant to UTC and labels it `UTC` (a fixed ASCII label, not the locale's zone name), so `2026-01-15T20:30Z` reads `Jan 15, 2026, 20:30 UTC` for every viewer instead of their own local time. Changing the zone re-stamps the ALREADY-RENDERED surfaces in place, with no reload: the comment cards, both sidebar metadata rows, the runtime footer, and an open in-document comment dialog (an in-progress dialog EDIT is left alone, so a draft is never discarded). Because the re-stamp rebuilds the comment list, it PUTS BACK the list's scroll position - a relabelling must not throw a reviewer reading deep in a long list to the top. The invariant is enforced at the WRITER, not at each call site: `setUtcTimes()` itself runs the one guard, which re-stamps only when the stored zone really differs from the one on screen and records the new zone only AFTER the re-stamp lands, so a failed refresh is retried rather than treated as current. The cross-document half - a `storage` event, which is deliberately NOT keyed on `e.key`, since a `localStorage.clear()` reports a null key and on `file://` every document shares one origin - is registered in `50-sidebar.js` beside the guard, so it still runs in a document whose COMMENT UI region has no Preferences rows. The storage manager's `Delete shared preferences` row owns this key and fires no `storage` event in its own document, so it calls the same guard; without that the footer would keep reading UTC beside cards drawn in local time. The Copy all bundle and the print appendix read the preference when they are BUILT, so they follow the reviewer's display zone (deliberately: the zone label makes each line unambiguous either way). An EXPORT reads it at neither end - Shareable / Offline / Plain HTML / standalone carry the raw ISO instant in the embedded store, so the recipient's own preference decides how it renders, and the Markdown export carries no comment timestamps at all. A refused preference write re-stamps nothing, since the stored zone did not change. | `tests/99-timestamp-zone.spec.js` - `CMH-MENU-PREF-11: turning UTC on re-labels every rendered timestamp without a reload`, `CMH-MENU-PREF-11: an OPEN comment dialog re-stamps in place when another tab changes the zone`, `CMH-MENU-PREF-11: a storage event that does not move the zone leaves the list alone`, `CMH-MENU-PREF-11: deleting the shared preferences re-stamps every surface back to local time`, `CMH-MENU-PREF-11: the Copy all bundle carries the UTC-labelled time`, `CMH-MENU-PREF-11: an exported copy carries the instant, not the exporter's zone`; source: `assets/js/50-sidebar.js` - `formatTime()`, `cmhRefreshTimeLabels()`, `cmhApplyTimeZoneChange()`; `assets/js/06-preferences.js` - `setUtcTimes()`, `cmhUtcTimesChanged()`; `assets/js/53-comment-popover.js` - `cmhRefreshCommentPopoverTime()`; `assets/js/57-storage-manager.js` |
## Rich-text comment notes

Review comment notes are stored as a plain-text markdown-ish SOURCE string and rendered to safe HTML
at display time (sidebar card, inline popover, print appendix). A composer formatting toolbar and
Ctrl/Cmd shortcuts make the markers discoverable, mimicking Office-style comments. Rendering is
presentation-only: the stored note is unchanged, so old notes stay compatible and Copy all preserves
the raw source.

| Feature id | Behavior | Covering tests |
| --- | --- | --- |
| CMH-RICH-01 | `renderRichNote` renders `**bold**`, `*italic*`, `__underline__`, `~~strike~~`, and inline-code markers as `<strong>`/`<em>`/`<u>`/`<s>`/`<code>` in the reviewer's sidebar card note (`.note.cmh-rich`). | `tests/33-rich-text.spec.js` - `renders bold, italic, underline, strikethrough, and inline code from markers in the sidebar card (CMH-RICH-01)` |
| CMH-RICH-02 | Lines beginning `- ` render as a `<ul class="cmh-rich-list">` bullet list, and the stored `comment.note` keeps the raw source (rendering is presentation-only). | `tests/33-rich-text.spec.js` - `renders '- ' lines as a bullet list and stores the note as raw source (CMH-RICH-02)` |
| CMH-RICH-03 | Markdown-style links (a label in square brackets followed by a URL in parentheses, including balanced parentheses in the URL) and bare `http(s)://` URLs (trailing sentence punctuation stripped) render as `<a target="_blank" rel="noopener noreferrer nofollow">`; clicking a rendered note link navigates without firing the card's jump/flash handler. | `tests/33-rich-text.spec.js` - `renders markdown links and bare-URL auto-links as safe new-tab anchors; a note link does not trigger the card jump (CMH-RICH-03)` |

A null note renders as an empty card. | `tests/33-rich-text.spec.js` - `escapes HTML and rejects javascript/data link schemes; malformed markers stay literal (CMH-RICH-04)`; `tests/33-rich-text.spec.js` - `renders hostile long input fast without hanging (CMH-RICH-04-dos)`; `tests/33-rich-text.spec.js` - `strips control chars so a link URL cannot be CR-obfuscated, and a null note renders empty (CMH-RICH-04-ctl)` |

## Authoring input sizing

Every surface a reviewer types a comment into (the floating composer, the side-pane inline
reply/edit editor, and the in-document comment dialog's editor) sizes itself to what is being
written, and is rendered at a readable size, so a long note never has to be composed inside a
two-line box.

| Feature id | Behavior | Covering tests |
| --- | --- | --- |
| CMH-GROW-01 | Every comment-authoring textarea AUTOGROWS to fit its content - the side-pane inline reply/edit editor, the floating comment composer, and the in-document dialog's editor. It grows as the reviewer types (no scrolling inside the box and no manual drag needed) and shrinks back whenever the content needs fewer lines, including a replacement that is LONGER in characters but wraps to fewer lines; the CSS `min-height` is the floor. Measuring a shrink never scrolls the comments panel under the reviewer, an editor opened or restored on EXISTING text (editing a saved note, or a draft carried across a re-render) comes back at content size rather than collapsed, and a measurement taken while the editor is not rendered yields no height, so it is retried rather than latched. | `tests/93-autogrow.spec.js` - `the side-pane reply input grows to fit what is typed and shrinks back (CMH-GROW-01)`, `a replacement that is longer but wraps to fewer lines still shrinks the box (CMH-GROW-01)`, `a restored draft comes back at content size, not collapsed (CMH-GROW-01)`, `an editor rebuilt while hidden still reaches content size once revealed (CMH-GROW-01)`, `shrinking a draft does not scroll the comments list under the reviewer (CMH-GROW-01)`, `an existing reply opens its editor already sized to the reply (CMH-GROW-01)`, `the floating composer textarea autogrows the same way (CMH-GROW-01)`, `the in-document popover editor autogrows too, and opens sized to the note (CMH-GROW-01)` |
| CMH-GROW-02 | Growth stops at each input's declared cap (`--cmh-grow-max`, a custom property this layer enforces rather than a CSS `max-height`, which would also bound the native resize handle; a missing or nonsensical value falls back to a default and no cap may exceed the viewport), after which the box SCROLLS instead of pushing Cancel/Save out of the card or dialog. A floating surface that grew after it was positioned (the composer, the in-document dialog) pulls itself back into the viewport on both axes, and stays viewport-sized even on a short screen, so its Save button is always reachable; a viewport change re-measures and re-clamps every open editor without waiting for a keystroke. A manual drag of the `resize: vertical` handle wins: an inline height the runtime did not write switches that editor to the reviewer's size, autogrow stops adjusting it, and that hand-picked size survives a sidebar re-render along with the draft - even when the drag was not followed by any typing. | `tests/93-autogrow.spec.js` - `growth stops at a cap and the box scrolls instead (CMH-GROW-02)`, `a grown composer stays fully on screen so Save is still reachable (CMH-GROW-02)`, `a grown in-document dialog stays fully on screen too (CMH-GROW-02)`, `a short viewport never leaves a grown composer taller than the screen (CMH-GROW-02)`, `a manual resize wins - autogrow stops for that editor (CMH-GROW-02)`, `a hand-sized reply editor keeps its height across a sidebar re-render (CMH-GROW-02)`, `a drag with no typing after it still survives a re-render (CMH-GROW-02)` |
| CMH-GROW-03 | The side-pane reply/edit input is rendered at the regular chrome font (`--cp-chrome-font`), the same size as the comment note it answers and as the floating composer - not the small metadata token used for timestamps and meta rows. | `tests/93-autogrow.spec.js` - `the reply input renders at the same font size as the composer (CMH-GROW-03)` |
