| CMH-REVIEW-16 | The `reviewedSections` block is resolved by the EMBEDDED COMMENTS region that OWNS it - the region's own BEGIN/END comment markers plus document order - among the blocks the CONTENT-ROOT BOUNDARY accepts (CMH-EXP-17), not by the first `getElementById` match, on BOTH the load and the export path, and only a `<script>` can carry it (exactly what the validator's shape check accepts, so the two cannot disagree about what the block is). A decoy block carrying the same id elsewhere is ignored on load and left with its own contents on export, while the region-owned block keeps taking the state; a document that owns no such block (an older file) still gets a fresh one inserted after its region-owned `embeddedComments` block. Resolution is deliberately conservative: markers that are ABSENT still let a LONE block resolve (a file upgraded from before the feature existed keeps working) - safe only because the boundary already dropped every candidate inside the content root, so an authored decoy can never BE that lone block, and a CONTESTED content root drops them all and resolves nothing, MALFORMED markers (not exactly one ordered pair document-wide, which is also a validator error, so a stray authored comment that quotes a marker line disables review rather than corrupting it) resolve nothing, and `<noscript>` contents are skipped on both paths because `DOMParser` (scripting disabled) parses them as real nodes while the live document does not - so the export can never write into a block the reader's browser treats as text. When nothing can be attributed to the region the export declines - it neither overwrites the decoy nor invents a third block, and it also declines to anchor a new block when more than one `embeddedComments` block the layer OWNS exists (a decoy inside the content root is not one of them, so it cannot veto the insert), since the comments themselves are written into the first one - and the reason travels back to the caller so the single download toast carries it, naming the ONE state it hit (every block inside the content root, a contested content root, several owned blocks, malformed markers, or a block outside the region) rather than listing every possible cause (a separate toast would be replaced by it); the load path warns the reader once, in a toast and in the console, from that SAME single diagnosis, so the reader's warning and the download toast can never disagree about what is wrong with the file - instead of silently showing every section unreviewed. `validate.py` reports both failure shapes - a duplicated `reviewedSections` id (like the other reserved state-block ids, CMH-VAL-01) and an id the region does not own (outside it, or not on a `<script>`) - and `mark_reviewed.py` refuses to write a block the region does not own. | `tests/90-section-review.spec.js` - `a decoy reviewedSections block cannot shadow the region-owned review state (CMH-REVIEW-16)`, `a content-region reviewedSections decoy is never read as the layer's block (CMH-EXP-17)`, `a contested content root leaves the review block unresolved (CMH-EXP-17)`, `a content-region embeddedComments decoy does not veto the review-state insert (CMH-EXP-17)`, `the export declines rather than writing a content-region decoy (CMH-EXP-17)`, `a document with no content root still resolves its review block (CMH-EXP-17)`, `a noscript decoy is invisible to both the load and the export (CMH-REVIEW-16)`, `absent region markers still resolve a lone block, malformed ones resolve nothing (CMH-REVIEW-16)`, `a document with no block gets one inserted inside the region (CMH-REVIEW-16)`, `export declines to bake review state when no block can be attributed to the region (CMH-REVIEW-16)`; `tests/test_validate_layer.py` - `ReviewedSectionsTests.test_duplicate_reviewed_sections_block_flagged`, `ReviewedSectionsTests.test_reviewed_sections_block_outside_the_region_flagged`; `tests/test_mark_reviewed.py` - `MarkReviewedTests.test_a_block_outside_the_embedded_comments_region_is_refused`, `MarkReviewedTests.test_malformed_region_markers_are_refused`, `MarkReviewedTests.test_a_block_inside_the_region_is_still_written` |
| CMH-REVIEW-17 | Section hashes are taken over the CANONICAL (authored source-order) content, exactly like the whole-document hash, so a reader's persisted table sort can neither flip an already-reviewed section to "changed" nor store a sorted-order hash when a section is marked reviewed while a table is sorted (which would then flip when the sort is cleared). The canonical order is READ, never restored by moving live rows: `_cmhScanSections()` walks the content root itself and, while a sort is active, visits a `<tbody>`'s rows in stamped `data-cmh-row` order permuted through their existing slots (so the authored inter-row whitespace still counts exactly once), leaving the DOM untouched. That matters because the scan runs on every sidebar/badge refresh: mutating the rows there would blur a focused control, collapse a live text selection mid-comment, and churn the table-scroll and widget observers. The runtime OWNS that index - `_indexTableRows()` re-stamps every sortable row with its position in the FILE before any persisted sort is applied - and only a body whose rows all carry the stamp is reordered, so an authored or stale `data-cmh-row` cannot silently re-order a table away from the source the Python hasher reads. | `tests/90-section-review.spec.js` - `a persisted table sort does not flip a reviewed section to changed (CMH-REVIEW-17)`, `computing review state never reorders the reader's rows or steals focus (CMH-REVIEW-17)`; source: `assets/js/84-section-review.js` - `_cmhScanSections()`, `_cmhCanonicalChildNodes()`, `computeSectionStates()` |

| CMH-THREAD-09 | An in-progress inline reply/edit draft (a reply, a reply edit, or a root-note edit) is preserved across a sidebar re-render (comment sort, a note-typing debounce, a checklist change, etc.) - the editor is re-opened with the same text rather than silently dropped - and still saves normally afterward. The reviewer's SELECTION is part of that draft: the re-opened editor restores the snapshotted `selectionStart`/`selectionEnd` instead of collapsing the caret to the end, so a re-render between selecting a word and clicking a formatting-toolbar button still wraps the word rather than appending bare markers. FOCUS is not: the snapshot records whether the editor owned focus (a deferred focus the open path has queued but not yet delivered counts as ownership), and the re-opened editor is only re-focused when it did, so a re-render triggered from elsewhere (a note the reviewer is typing into, a checklist tick, the Sort button) restores the text and selection without pulling the caret out of the control actually in use. When focus was on the editor's own formatting toolbar or its Save/Cancel button - an element the re-render destroys - it is handed back to the rebuilt equivalent control rather than dropped into the textarea. An open MODAL dialog (Manage storage, the clear-all confirm, Help) vetoes that ownership outright for the whole rebuild: the side pane sits BEHIND the dialog's overlay, so the re-opened editor keeps its text and selection but is never focused - focus there would escape the ``aria-modal`` dialog's trap into a control the reviewer can neither see nor reach - the veto is enforced at DELIVERY time too - the editor's deferred focus timer, the post-save hand-back, and an editor's close-restore all stand down while a dialog is up - so a focus armed before the dialog opened cannot land behind it either, and that deferred focus is HELD rather than dropped, so once the dialog closes the reviewer is left on a real control instead of stranded. Focus found BEHIND the overlay (stranded on ``<body>``, in the side pane, or moved out into the document by a delete run FROM the dialog, which restores focus to a composer's opener) is handed back to the dialog, preferring the dialog's own declared safe default (``.cm-modal-default``/``[autofocus]`` - the clear-all confirm's Cancel, the storage manager's inline-confirm Cancel, Help's search field) over raw DOM order so a destructive confirm button is never made the Enter-default, skipping any candidate that cannot actually take focus and falling back to the dialog box itself. Focus the reviewer genuinely holds inside the dialog, or on chrome that paints ABOVE the overlay (a toast, the deck's own controls), is left alone. The same rule covers every ``aria-modal`` dialog this layer builds - Manage storage, the clear-all confirm, and Help - because it is keyed on the rendered overlay rather than on any one dialog's state flag. Re-clicking the edit action on an editor that is already open only re-focuses it, keeping the live selection and its anchor direction. | `tests/92-threads.spec.js` - `an in-progress inline reply draft survives a re-render such as sorting (CMH-THREAD-09)`, `an in-progress ROOT edit draft survives a re-render (CMH-THREAD-09)`, `a re-render preserves the draft's SELECTION, so the formatting toolbar still wraps it (CMH-THREAD-09)`, `a re-render triggered from elsewhere leaves focus where the reviewer put it (CMH-THREAD-09)`; `tests/72-storage.spec.js` - `deleting a comment from the manager keeps focus in the dialog with an inline draft open (CMH-THREAD-09)`, `a re-render while a modal is up never hands focus to the pane behind it (CMH-THREAD-09)`, `a re-render while a modal is up leaves focus on the dialog control the reviewer is using (CMH-THREAD-09)`, `a deferred editor focus armed before a modal opens is not delivered behind it (CMH-THREAD-09)`, `a stranded focus is handed to the confirm dialog's SAFE default, not its danger button (CMH-THREAD-09)`, `focus parked in the document behind an open dialog is pulled back into it (CMH-THREAD-09)`, `the Help dialog gets the same modal focus veto as the storage manager (CMH-THREAD-09)`, `closing an inline editor while a modal is up hands focus to the dialog, not the pane (CMH-THREAD-09)`, `a deferred editor focus held behind a modal is delivered once the dialog closes (CMH-THREAD-09)` |

Save stores the note with an `updatedAt` stamp, marks the card `(edited)` and returns focus to the card's `edit` button; Cancel or Escape discards. A click inside any inline editor (its textarea, Save or Cancel) never also fires the card's jump-to-anchor fall-through, so the reader's place in the document is kept. A comment is editable in exactly one place at a time: if the same note is already open in the in-document dialog (or a floating composer from re-selecting its text), the panel hands the reader back to that editor when it holds unsaved text instead of opening a second one whose save would overwrite it. | `tests/92-threads.spec.js` - `editing a ROOT comment edits IN the sidebar card without jumping to the anchor (CMH-THREAD-10)`; `tests/09-interactions.spec.js` - `editing a comment updates its note and marks it edited`, `CMH-CORE-16: a dirty in-place edit is not swallowed, switched away, or duplicated (CMH-THREAD-10)`, `CMH-CORE-16: a dirty panel edit is not duplicated by the in-document dialog (CMH-THREAD-10)`, `CMH-CORE-16: the dialog defers to an open floating edit composer for the same note (CMH-THREAD-10)`, `CMH-CORE-16: a dirty inline draft is not duplicated by the floating composer (CMH-THREAD-10)`; source: `assets/js/50-sidebar.js` - `openInlineNoteEdit()` |
| CMH-THREAD-11 | Focus survives a re-render of the comment list. `renderComments()` replaces the whole list, so a control the reviewer is on - the checklist, note, and board change cards' `reset` buttons, and the comment (`del`) and reply (`reply-del`) delete confirms - is destroyed by the very render it triggered, and the reviewer used to be dropped on `<body>` with no way back but tabbing in from the top of the page. EVERY render notes where focus was before it rebuilds and hands it back afterwards, so this holds however the render is reached - synchronously from the click, a frame later through the board's mutation observer, or twice over when two renders are queued - rather than depending on each handler to remember. Focus goes to the equivalent rebuilt control (matched by the owning reply entry or card's identity plus the same `data-act`); else to whichever control took its index in the rebuilt list and then outwards from there, so a candidate that still refuses focus hands off to its neighbour rather than to the top of a long list; and finally to the list container itself (`#commentList`, `role="region"` + `aria-label="Comments list"`, `tabindex="-1"`, carrying its own inset focus ring), so an emptied list still lands the reviewer on the panel rather than on `<body>`. A candidate that cannot actually take focus is skipped rather than silently swallowing the restore, since `focus()` is a no-op on a hidden, disabled, or inert element and the comment filter hides non-matching cards outright; the index is taken over that same filtered sequence, so cards the filter hides cannot shift it and push the restore onto a distant control. Only focus that was INSIDE the list is carried: a render triggered from outside it (a note being typed, a checklist ticked in the document, the Sort button) leaves the caret exactly where it is, an inline editor's focus is carried by its own draft snapshot instead (CMH-THREAD-09, including a deferred focus that snapshot has queued, and the save paths that focus their own rebuilt control), and a rebuild that stranded nobody changes nothing. Focus is restored with `preventScroll`, so the reader's place in the document is not moved. | `tests/92-threads.spec.js` - `a Reset change card that re-renders the panel hands focus to a rebuilt control (CMH-THREAD-11)`, `a board Reset card whose re-render lands a frame later still hands focus back (CMH-THREAD-11)`, `deleting a comment hands focus to the card that took its place (CMH-THREAD-11)`, `deleting a reply hands focus back into the surviving thread card (CMH-THREAD-11)`, `resetting the last change in an otherwise empty panel focuses the list itself (CMH-THREAD-11)`, `a re-render driven from a document control leaves focus there, not in the panel (CMH-THREAD-11)`, `a delete the reviewer sits on before confirming still hands focus back (CMH-THREAD-11)`, `a competing re-render does not swallow the board Reset's restore (CMH-THREAD-11)`, `with a filter hiding every survivor, focus lands on the list, not a hidden control (CMH-THREAD-11)`, `an inline draft open elsewhere does not swallow the restore (CMH-THREAD-11)`, `a control whose own card survives the render gets the focus back (CMH-THREAD-11)`, `cards the filter hides do not push the restore onto a distant control (CMH-THREAD-11)`; source: `assets/js/50-sidebar.js` - `_captureListFocus()`, `_restoreListFocus()` |

| CMH-PICK-01 | Every side-pane comment card carries an obvious `Select` control in its meta row - a real `<input type="checkbox">` inside its label, so it is keyboard-operable and announced as a checkbox for free, with an `aria-label` naming the comment it picks (`Select comment #N`). A selection bar appears under the panel's primary row announcing the live count (`N comments selected`, `aria-live="polite"`), and because that live region is refreshed after EVERY render (a sort, a checklist tick, a note keystroke) it is written only when the text actually CHANGES, so an unchanged count is never re-announced while the reviewer is doing something else. With no selection the controls read `Copy all` and the bar is hidden, so the all-or-nothing default is unchanged. | `tests/99-comment-selection.spec.js` - `a selection relabels the copy control to Copy selected and counts itself (CMH-PICK-02)`, `the live count is written only when it actually changes (CMH-PICK-02)` |

Unselected comments appear nowhere in the bundle. | `tests/99-comment-selection.spec.js` - `Copy selected emits only the selected threads, replies included (CMH-PICK-03)` |
| CMH-PICK-04 | A partial hand-back declares itself: the bundle carries a `Scope: selected comments only (N of M open comment threads)` line right after `Source:`, so the agent never reads a missing comment as already handled. A selection is a COMMENT-only scope - the tracked widget-layout, checklist, and editable-note change sections are omitted and their machine-trailer state stays canonical `{}`, because those changes are not selectable and must not ride along on a partial hand-back. Because that canonical `{}` cannot say "withheld" apart from "nothing pending", a further `Withheld:` line names the tracked change KINDS that DO exist and were held back - and it appears only when such changes genuinely exist, so it never becomes noise the agent learns to skip. With no selection the same document still hands every tracked change back exactly as before, with neither line. | `tests/99-comment-selection.spec.js` - `a partial hand-back declares its scope and carries no tracked note change (CMH-PICK-04)`, `a partial hand-back with nothing withheld says so by staying silent (CMH-PICK-04)` |

When that button HELD focus, clearing hands focus to a still-visible control first (`Copy all`) rather than dropping it on `<body>`, because clearing hides the bar the button lives in and `.cm-skip [hidden]` removes it from layout - the same contract every other vanishing control in this panel keeps (CMH-THREAD-11). The floating toolbar's overflow menu carries the same item (`#btnClearSelectionTop`, hidden until a selection exists, sitting between `Save as PDF` and `Manage storage` so the data-management pair stays adjacent per CMH-UI-13), because with the panel collapsed that menu is the only chrome a reviewer has and a `Copy selected` button they can neither inspect nor undo is a dead end; it restores focus to the menu's own trigger, exactly like `Clear all comments`. | `tests/99-comment-selection.spec.js` - `Clear selection deselects everything and deletes nothing (CMH-PICK-05)`, `Clear selection hands focus to a still-visible control (CMH-PICK-05)`, `the collapsed toolbar can inspect and clear a selection too (CMH-PICK-05)`, `picking and clearing never re-render the list, so an open draft survives (CMH-PICK-01, CMH-PICK-05)` |
| CMH-PICK-06 | The sidebar `More` menu grows a `Clear selected comments` item that is HIDDEN unless a selection exists. Activating it confirms first through the same `showConfirm` dialog Clear all uses (naming the comments AND the replies that go with them, cancel-by-default, Escape cancels), then deletes only the selected threads - root and replies together - tombstoning every id so the whole thread stays deleted across a reload, closing any editor or dialog left showing a removed id, dropping the highlights, and saving, while every unselected comment is left intact. Focus returns to the still-visible `More` trigger. | `tests/99-comment-selection.spec.js` - `Clear selected comments shows only with a selection and deletes only those (CMH-PICK-06)`; `tests/72-followups.spec.js` - `the side pane search row, dropdown menu items and card edit action are >=44px touch targets on mobile (CMH-RESP-15)`, `enlarging the side pane's controls does not starve the comment list on a landscape phone (CMH-RESP-14)` |

## Content, visual conventions, KQL, charts, and optional loaders

| Feature id | Behavior | Covering tests |
| --- | --- | --- |
| CMH-THEME-01 | The template defaults to light theme; `?clawpilotTheme=dark` forces dark; `?clawpilotTheme=auto` follows OS preference. | `tests/01-inline.spec.js` - `renders in a light theme by default`; `tests/10-more.spec.js` - `renders and works in dark theme (clawpilotTheme=dark)`; `tests/33-coverage-gaps.spec.js` - `clawpilotTheme=auto follows the OS color scheme (CMH-THEME-01)`; `tests/23-coverage.spec.js` - `CMH-THEME-01: template defaults to light, supports dark, and follows OS for auto` |
| CMH-THEME-02 | The flat-doc validator evaluates authored `--cp-*` theme overrides for WCAG readability, resolving the light (`:root`) and dark (`[data-theme="dark"]`) environments SEPARATELY (a token overridden only in dark is judged against its dark value, matching custom-property cascade). It runs only on tokens the author changed from the shipped defaults, so the accepted defaults are never flagged. Graduated severity: text/link pairs use a 4.5:1 target - a near-miss in the 3.0-4.49 band is an advisory WARNING, below 3.0:1 is an ERROR; non-text UI pairs use a 3.0:1 bar (below it is an ERROR). A chain that cannot be resolved to two concrete colors is reported as an 'unresolved / not evaluated' advisory. This is a STATIC resolution, NOT a computed-style/cascade simulation (documented non-goal). `--suggest` prints a compliant nudged foreground for a finding when one is reachable (unresolved and mid-tone-unreachable findings get a diagnostic instead). A `<style data-cmh-brand>` palette is deferred to the `--brand` tooling's own contrast advisory (CMH-TOOL-19) and not double-flagged here. The near-miss and unresolved advisories carry a stable prefix so `retrofit.py` keeps them out of its hard-fail path; a bad-contrast ERROR still blocks retrofit. | CMH-CONTENT-08 | Table sorting is numeric-aware with empty cells first and no `NaN` comparisons; sort state persists to `localStorage`, re-applies before comment restore, recomputes live text offsets after sort, drops stale offsets when a multi-row highlight becomes discontiguous, reports unavailable offsets in Copy all for that invalidated text anchor, and canonicalizes comments back to original row order for export. A table's persisted key is bound ONCE, on the UNSORTED startup DOM, and looked up by ELEMENT after that (a later pass never re-keys a table it already bound): the key is positional, and a sortable table nested in another table's cell changes document index whenever the outer table's rows move, so the call sites otherwise disagreed - `applyPersistedTableSorts` keys on the unsorted load DOM while `setupSortableTables` runs AFTER the persisted sorts are applied (an already-sorted DOM). A reader who sorted a nested table persisted it under a key neither reload nor export looked it up by, so that sort was silently dropped; binding once makes them agree, and for a document with no nested sortable table the bound value is what every call site already computed, so no reader loses a persisted sort. A table added after startup is never bound and falls back to the positional key - a defensive path only, since sort controls are wired once at startup. Persisted state is accepted only when it can actually be applied (`_validSortState`: a non-negative INTEGER `col` and a `dir` of exactly `asc`/`desc`), by both the load pass and the control setup that reflects the direction on the chevron, so a corrupt entry cannot announce a sort that is not applied; the load pass replays INNERMOST-FIRST, because an outer table sorted on a column whose cells hold a nested table ranks its rows by that cell's text and would otherwise be ranked against nested tables not yet back in their own order, and one table that cannot be sorted is skipped rather than aborting the rest of startup. Innermost-first replay alone reproduces only the NATURAL click order (sort the nested table, then the outer one): a reader who sorted the outer table FIRST and the nested one second had ranked the outer rows against the nested table's OLD order, and nothing re-ranked an ancestor when a descendant moved, so the replay handed back an order the reader never saw (#1053). A sort-control click therefore RE-APPLIES every sortable ANCESTOR's persisted sort, nearest first (each ancestor's own move in turn re-ranks the next one out, so a three-level nesting re-ranks the outermost table too, not just the nearest), unsorting an ancestor before re-sorting it because `_sortRows` breaks ties on a row's CURRENT index while the replay always sorts from the authored order - so the live view is exactly the answer the replay produces, for either click order, and a reload and an export both reproduce it. Clearing a nested sort is the same class of change and re-ranks its ancestors too. The rejected alternative, making an outer sort key invariant to descendant row order, would rank a column holding nothing but a nested table as EMPTY - a worse surprise than the mismatch it fixes. Re-ranking an ancestor permutes the row that HOLDS the clicked table, and the slot swap detaches and re-inserts it - taking the chevron the reader just pressed with it and dropping focus to `<body>` - so the click handler restores focus to the control it actuated (nothing else moves it: a table's own chevrons live in its `<thead>`, which is never permuted), and deliberately WITHOUT `preventScroll`, since the control physically moved and pinning the viewport could leave the focused chevron off-screen. An ancestor whose re-sort throws is left UNSORTED rather than put back, which is what the load replay does with a sort that throws, so the live view still agrees with a reload. The export pass captures each table's LIVE ROW ORDER before its first unsort and puts exactly that order back (via `_reorderBody`), never an order re-derived by re-sorting: `_sortRows` breaks ties on a row's current index and reads nested-table text, so a re-sort could hand the reader an order they never had. It restores only the tables it actually unsorted, and puts BOTH the row order and the reader's live comment offsets back from a `finally` (offsets restored from a snapshot rather than recomputed, so unwinding cannot throw a second time and mask the real failure). Without that, a throw part-way through the canonical recompute left the reader with every table unsorted, or holding authored-order offsets that the next ordinary save persisted and the next load anchored onto an unrelated row. | `tests/24-copy-sort.spec.js` - `sorting keeps comment anchors attached, and the sort survives reload`, `a scattered multi-row table highlight does not restore onto unrelated rows after reload (CMH-CONTENT-08)`, `a sortable table nested in a sorted table keeps its own sort across an export (CMH-CONTENT-08)`, `a throw during the export canonical pass never strands the reader's tables unsorted (CMH-CONTENT-08)`, `a failed export leaves the reader's live comment offsets untouched (CMH-CONTENT-08)`, `persisted sorts replay innermost-first, so an outer sort keyed on a nested table survives a reload (CMH-CONTENT-08)`, `sorting a nested table re-applies its ancestor's persisted sort, so either click order replays the same (CMH-CONTENT-08)`, `a nested sort re-ranks every sortable ancestor, not just the nearest (CMH-CONTENT-08)`; `tests/28-duck-fixes.spec.js` - `sorting a numeric column with multiple empty cells does not scramble (NaN guard)`, `a comment on a sorted table cell exports with a correct anchor`; source: `assets/js/` - `_sortRows()`, `_tableKeyFor()`, `_validSortState()`, `_reapplyAncestorSorts()`, `_canonicalCommentsForExport()` |

The "already has a title" check parses the fragment (it does not scan raw text), so an `<h1>` inside an HTML comment, `<script>`, or `<style>`, or an `h1`/`cmh-lede` nested below the top level, does not suppress the prepended title. The validator's own title requirement for a title-bearing kind (`report`/`plan`) reads the same way: a title is VISIBLE text, so an `<h1>` whose text is only whitespace, C0/C1 controls, DEL, format characters (a zero-width space, a bidi mark, a BOM) or unassigned/noncharacter code points does NOT satisfy it, and neither does an empty lede header. That predicate is explicit because a TEXT character reference is decoded by the browser rule rather than deleted by `html.unescape` (CMH-VAL-21), so `<h1>&#1;</h1>` would otherwise pass as a title nobody can see; U+FFFD is deliberately visible, since a browser draws the replacement glyph. | `tests/46-heading-a11y-title.spec.js` - `the document title h1 is themed and visibly larger than body prose`; `tests/test_new_document.py` - `DocTitleTests` incl. `test_ensure_doc_title_ignores_h1_inside_comment`, `test_ensure_doc_title_ignores_h1_inside_script`, `test_ensure_doc_title_ignores_nested_h1_and_lede`; `tests/test_validate_doc_boundaries.py` - `test_an_invisible_title_does_not_satisfy_the_title_requirement`; `tests/test_validate_kind.py` - `test_report_without_h1_errors`, `test_report_with_h1_is_clean`, `test_report_with_empty_lede_errors`; source: `assets/css/` - `#commentRoot > h1`, `#commentRoot > header > h1`; `tools/authoring/new_document.py` - `ensure_doc_title()`, `_has_active_title()`; `tools/validate/checks/kind.py` - `visible_text()` |
| CMH-CONTENT-16 | The reviewable content region is exactly the `#commentRoot` subtree, and the prose view excludes what is INERT inside it: `generate_toc.py` and `validate.py` both track the root by identity and mark it closed on the root's (or an ancestor's) end tag, so headings and prose cross-references in a later sibling container (for example a page `<footer>` after `</main id=commentRoot>`) are not collected into the TOC nor validated as content, even though they sit at the same nesting depth. A `<template>` body is inert for the same reason a later sibling is outside: its contents live in a DocumentFragment a browser never renders, so `_DocParser` collects no prose from one - whether the template is closed or left open at end of input, where it stays inert to EOF - and a template nested inside an open heading contributes none of its text to that heading either (a reader sees `Real` in `<h2>Real<template>Hidden</template></h2>`, so the named cross-reference, document-title and TOC-generation paths must too - `generate_toc.py` applies the same rule, and a heading whose text is ENTIRELY inside a template is listed by neither, which correctly leaves a `report`/`plan` whose only `<h1>` is parked in a template failing the title requirement). One known, deliberate limit: it is about the PROSE and HEADING views, not every prose-ish check, so each other pass with its own parser needs its own guard (the density / wall-of-prose pass grew one under CMH-VAL-15, issue #956). An end tag written inside a template no longer pops it early either - CMH-VAL-21 gave every tolerant parser the template scoping floor (issue #957), so `<p><template>parked</p>` keeps the rest of the fragment inert exactly as a browser does. The shape most easily missed is a template-parked RAW-TEXT element: `_cur_script`/`_cur_style` are deliberately not set inside a template (a parked block is neither live script nor live CSS, and its body belongs in the template-only views the offline checks read, CMH-OFFLINE-04), so a parked `<script>`/`<style>` body reaches `handle_data` with NEITHER set and would otherwise fall straight through into the prose view as if the author had typed its source as words - the parked block's text is REGRESSION-LOCKED directly on the parser, in the prose view and in the template-only views, rather than only through the checks that read them (the exclusion itself is earlier work; what this row adds is the pin, so the raw-text shape cannot come back unnoticed). The mermaid SOURCE view follows the same rule (issue #962): a `<template>` nested inside a LIVE mermaid host (`pre.mermaid` / `div.mermaid`) contributes none of its parked text to the diagram source `check_mermaid_syntax` reads - whether the template is closed or left open to EOF - because a template's children live in its `.content` DocumentFragment and are therefore not part of the host's `textContent`, which is exactly what mermaid renders from (a declarative shadow root is the one `<template>` a browser DOES render, and it needs no carve-out here: its content becomes a SHADOW tree, which is still outside the host's `textContent`, so mermaid never reads it either). That view reads the NAMESPACE-AWARE HTML-template floor CMH-VAL-21 already keeps (`_in_html_template()`), and so does the INERTNESS floor `_in_template()` under it (issue #1035): the inert-ancestor count used to be keyed on the tag NAME alone, so `<math><template>text</template></math>` inside `#commentRoot` - an ordinary unknown foreign element a browser keeps in the DOM and in its ancestor's `textContent`, and whose `<script>`/`<style>` it still runs or applies - was inert at once to the prose / unlinked-cross-reference view, the heading capture, the element view (`_record`) and the mermaid source view, and its raw-text children were PARKED in the template-only views rather than classified as they would be without that wrapper - which for an SVG `<script>`/`<style>`, the one case with unambiguous browser semantics (`SVGScriptElement` executes, `SVGStyleElement` applies), hid a genuinely live body from the checks that read the live views. (Whether the layer views should treat a MathML `<script>` - which executes in no browser - as live at all is a separate, pre-existing namespace question, issue #1101; this row only settles that the foreign `template` wrapper changes nothing either way.) Only an HTML-namespaced, non-shadow `<template>` counts now, so an element merely NAMED `template` in a foreign namespace hides no prose, no heading text, no id and no broken diagram source, while the rule cuts both ways: a `<template>` under an HTML integration point (`<svg><foreignObject>`, `<math><mi>`, an `<annotation-xml encoding="text/html">`) or after a foreign BREAKOUT start tag is HTML-namespaced and stays inert, and `shadowrootmode` on a foreign `template` attaches nothing. The two floors stay DISTINCT: `_in_template()` is inertness (a declarative shadow root is rendered, so it is not inert), and `_in_html_template()` is the textContent view, which is inertness OR a shadow tree. `generate_toc.py` keeps the same namespace rule in its own shadow-frame model. Live text around the template is still checked, and a host whose ONLY text is parked is correctly reported as an EMPTY block (mermaid's "No diagram type detected"), which is what a browser renders. `_record()` already declined to register a mermaid host that is itself inside a template, so both directions now agree. Without that, a document that merely SHOWS a cross reference inside a template (a doc about authoring, or any parked markup fragment) raised an unlinked-cross-reference warning its author could not clear by any edit to the rendered page, and the prose view disagreed with `_record()` and the heading capture, which already decline template content. | `tests/test_generate_toc.py` - `test_headings_after_root_close_are_ignored`, `test_heading_text_inside_a_template_is_not_part_of_the_title`, `test_a_heading_whose_text_is_only_a_template_is_not_listed`; | CMH-CONTENT-19 | A shipped `.cmh-diagram-gallery` layout helper lays out MULTIPLE diagrams of very different aspect ratios robustly, so authors do not hand-roll a fragile per-document grid. Above the mobile breakpoint it is a centred FLEX-WRAP of UNIFORM DIAGRAM-HEIGHT, content-HUGGING framed cards: every diagram is rendered at one fixed HEIGHT (`svg{height:15rem}`) with its WIDTH derived from the mermaid viewBox aspect ratio (`width:auto`, `!important` overriding mermaid's inline max-width, the `70-kql.css` `max-width:none` reset, and the layer's narrow cap; NO max-width clamp, so the diagram renders at its natural readable width), and each card SHRINKS to hug that width up to a generous `max-width:min(100%,48rem)`. So every diagram fills its card in BOTH dimensions: a tall-narrow diagram gets a narrow full-height card, a wide diagram gets a wide card, and a small diagram is scaled UP to the fixed height (never left tiny, marooned, slivered, or letterboxed). Sizing is pure deterministic CSS anchored on a definite height, so it is pixel-identical across Chromium/Firefox/WebKit and has no JS-measurement race; the layer's own narrow/wide scale-up (CMH-MMD-10, `updateMermaidWidthClass`) is additionally DISABLED inside the gallery - it is measurement-timing dependent and rendered diagrams tiny in a real browser (passing headless). Only diagram CONTAINERS are framed (`> pre.mermaid, > div.mermaid, > figure`), not `> *`, so a stray table/list is left alone; a `<figure>` card is `width:fit-content` so it hugs its diagram for a short caption and grows only to a bounded readable width (`figcaption{max-width:22rem}`) for a longer one, with `margin-inline:auto` centring both the diagram and the caption - so a long caption neither stretches the card to its full length (marooning the diagram) nor collapses to the tiny diagram width (towering into a narrow vertical strip); the `<figcaption>` is centred below, and when a wide diagram makes the figure its own horizontal scroll container the caption stays pinned in view via the RTL-safe logical `inset-inline-start`. Because a captioned figure's TOTAL card height includes its variable-height caption, the uniformity guarantee is on the DIAGRAM height (every card's diagram is the same 15rem), not on a captioned figure's whole card height. A diagram WIDER than the card cap keeps its full readable height and SCROLLS horizontally (`overflow-x:auto`, and `align-items:flex-start` so an over-wide diagram's START edge stays reachable by scrolling rather than being centred to a negative offset and clipped off-screen; start-alignment is visually identical for a diagram that fits, and needs no `safe` keyword so it works in every browser); an overflowing card gets a SCROLL affordance layered on top of its comment tab stop (WCAG 2.1.1): `markGalleryCardScrollable` adds, for a bare `pre`/`div` card, `role=group`, and gives every overflowing card the scroll hint as `aria-description` (never `aria-label`, so it never clobbers the comment accessible name owned by CMH-MMD-11), while a captioned `<figure>` keeps its implicit figure role - the helper NEVER touches `tabindex`/`aria-label`/`data-cmh-comment-a11y` (the comment tab stop, `makeMermaidCommentFocusable`, owns those unconditionally); the scroll `role`/`aria-description` are cleared when it no longer overflows, leaving the comment tab stop intact. At `<=480px` the helper is a single-column flow so the layer's natural diagram flow / wide scroll (CMH-RESP-01) is intact; print stacks it single-column and unframed (`92-print.css`). | `tests/53-more-examples.spec.js` - `gallery renders every diagram whole and well-filled in hugging uniform-height cards - no tiny, no sliver, no clip, no marooning` (describe `commentable visuals matrix: diagram gallery layout (CMH-DEMO-06 / CMH-CONTENT-19)`); | CMH-CONTENT-20 | Sorting a table is TEXT-NEUTRAL: `_reorderBody()` permutes the `<tr>` rows through their EXISTING slots (placeholder swap) instead of appending them to the `<tbody>`, so the whitespace text nodes an author leaves BETWEEN rows stay where they are. Without this, one sort stranded every inter-row whitespace node ahead of the rows, making the rows textually adjacent - a change no later unsort could undo, so a reader's persisted sort permanently drifted the document and section content hashes and the same file falsely showed the "not validated" banner (CMH-STAMP-03/05) on the machine where a table had been sorted and not on another. The row slots come from `body.rows`, the same collection every caller derives its order from, so the two are the same set by construction; a caller that ever breaks that (a length mismatch, or a row that is not a child of this body) gets a NO-OP rather than the append that caused the bug, and an identity reorder returns before touching the DOM (the canonical-hash and export passes unsort every sortable table, including untouched ones). | `tests/64-validation-banner.spec.js` - `a persisted sort of a whitespace-formatted table does not falsely invalidate the stamp`; `tests/24-copy-sort.spec.js` - `sorting and unsorting a whitespace-formatted table leaves the document text unchanged (CMH-CONTENT-20)`; source: `assets/js/62-sortable-tables.js` - `_reorderBody()` |

| CMH-HL-01 | The runtime highlights a commentable `<pre><code class="language-XXX">` block that shipped without highlight spans, on load, using the in-page tokenizer (the same `cmh-code-*` classes as the author-time highlighter), so a labelled block never renders as plain monochrome text even when the author never baked highlighting. It runs before the line-number gutter and before comment restoration, so line numbers and text-offset anchoring stay consistent (a comment on a now-highlighted block round-trips through reload). It is idempotent (an already-highlighted block is left alone) and only fires for a language the tokenizer knows (`diffLangKnown`); the known set includes the markup and xml families, so a raw `language-html`/`language-xml` block also self-heals (tag names, attribute-value strings, and `<!-- -->` comments), while an unknown/non-tokenizable label (`language-text`, `language-kusto`) stays plain. | `tests/61-code-highlight-fallback.spec.js` - `a language-labelled block with no spans is highlighted on load; unknown labels stay plain`, `an unbaked language-html and language-xml block is highlighted on load (markup and xml families) (CMH-HL-01)`, `an already-highlighted (baked) block is not re-highlighted`, `a comment on a runtime-highlighted code block survives reload`; source: `assets/js/` - `highlightCodeBlocks()` |
| CMH-HL-03 | The runtime tokenizer (`diffLangKnown` / `_HL_FAMILY` in `assets/js/26-highlight.js`) knows every language the author-time highlighter supports - every `highlight_code.LANGUAGE_CONFIGS` key AND every `highlight_code.ALIASES` key - so a supported language authored raw is always highlightable at runtime (via CMH-HL-01 and the diff highlighter) and can never silently render monochrome. Aliases are covered because the runtime resolves nothing: `diffLangKnown()` looks the RAW `language-XXX` label up in `_HL_FAMILY`, so an alias missing there renders monochrome even though the author-time tool highlights it (the defect that shipped `language-jsonc` as plain text). A drift guard fails the moment an author-time language or alias is added without runtime coverage, and a second guard fails in the REVERSE direction - a label the runtime knows but the tool does not would bake as plain text, and (since a markdown fence picks its nested language from this same table, CMH-HL-07/08) would nest on one path and stay opaque on the other. Keeping the two sets identical is what makes the nested-fence language a shared decision. Knowing the language is not enough on its own: every family that `_hlTokenRe()` gives its own comment/string patterns to is 1:1 with an author-time language, so it also carries its own KEYWORD set in `_HL_FAM_KW` mirroring that language's `LANGUAGE_CONFIGS[lang]["keywords"]` EXACTLY - and a family may only group languages that agree, so `xml` is its OWN family rather than riding along with html: it has a much smaller tag vocabulary and, unlike html, matches case-SENSITIVELY, so the merged family used to color `<div>` and `<ROOT>` in an XML block that the baked output leaves plain. Sharing the broad multi-language `_HL_KW_SET` both UNDER-colored a family (an unbaked `language-sql` block rendered `SELECT`/`INSERT`/`JOIN`/`GROUP`/`ORDER` plain while the baked block colored them, and `css`, `batch`, `powershell`, `haskell` and `lua` had the same gap) and OVER-colored it (`class` in Lua, `def` in Haskell - words the author-time tool never treats as keywords there). Only the genuinely multi-language buckets (`hash`, `c`) keep the shared set, `markdown` has no keywords, and the shared set is never WIDENED to close a family gap - a word only a dedicated family uses, such as `insert`, must stay a plain identifier in C, Python and everywhere else. (`select` is deliberately NOT the example: bash has a `select` loop, so it is legitimately shared vocabulary rather than SQL-only, and the guard is derived from the configs precisely so that distinction is made by the data rather than by hand.) Case rules mirror the author-time `CASE_INSENSITIVE_LANGUAGES` family by family (`sql`, `css`, `powershell`, `batch` and html-`markup` case-insensitive; `xml`, `json`, `lua`, `haskell` case-sensitive), since the runtime lowercases a token exactly when its family regex carries the `i` flag. The shared set is also kept HONEST in the other direction: every word in it must be a keyword of some language that actually uses it (`deriving`, `newtype` and `none` were left over from before Haskell and CSS had their own sets, and only mis-colored identifiers elsewhere). The shared bucket itself stays knowingly APPROXIMATE - one list cannot be exact for 23 languages, so it still colors, say, a lowercase `true` in Python that the author-time tool leaves plain; the guard pins that it carries nothing a dedicated family owns, not that it is per-language exact. A structural guard parses the runtime sets and compares them to the author-time configs, and fails if a future dedicated family has no set of its own. | `tests/test_highlight_parity.py` - `test_runtime_knows_every_author_time_language`, `test_runtime_knows_every_author_time_alias`, `test_author_time_knows_every_runtime_label`, `test_every_dedicated_family_has_its_own_keyword_set`, `test_the_dedicated_families_and_their_token_patterns_agree`, `test_each_family_keyword_set_matches_the_author_time_config`, `test_each_family_matches_the_author_time_case_sensitivity`, `test_the_shared_keyword_set_is_not_widened`, `test_python_tool_matches_the_shared_parity_fixture`; `tests/57-highlight-parity.spec.js` - `the runtime diff highlighter matches the shared parity fixture (GH-REGRESS-HIGHLIGHT-PARITY)`; `tests/61-code-highlight-fallback.spec.js` - `an unbaked language-sql block colors its own keywords, not the shared set's (CMH-HL-03)`; source: `assets/js/26-highlight.js` - `_HL_FAMILY`, `_HL_FAM_KW` |
| CMH-HL-05 | JSON is tokenized as JSON rather than as a generic C-family language, on both the author-time and the runtime path, and `jsonc` is a first-class label (an alias to `json` at author time, a known `_HL_FAMILY`/`_EXT_LANG` key at runtime, so a `language-jsonc` block is baked and self-heals instead of rendering monochrome). A property KEY - a double-quoted string whose next non-whitespace character is `:` - gets its own `cmh-code-key` token, so a key is tinted apart from a string VALUE the way every mainstream JSON highlighter renders it; a string value, a key-like string inside a comment, and every non-JSON language are unaffected (`KEY_STRING_LANGUAGES` is JSON-only). Both JSONC comment forms (`//` and `/* */`) are comments on both paths, and the runtime `json` family accepts only double-quoted strings and the three JSON barewords (`true`/`false`/`null`). (The diff highlighter tokenizes each diff line independently - a pre-existing property of that path - so within a diff a block comment SPANNING lines only colors its first line, and a key whose `:` sits on the NEXT line stays a string rather than a key; a whole `<pre>` block is tokenized in one pass and is unaffected.) | CMH-HL-06 | The author-time tokenizer's greedy operator run can never swallow the language's OWN comment opener, so a comment that directly abuts an operator with no whitespace between them (`{/* c */}`, `x=1;//n`, `f x={-c-}`, `$a=1<#c#>`, `x=1--c`) is still recognized as a comment instead of having its opener absorbed into the operator and its BODY highlighted as live code. | CMH-HL-08 | The runtime mirrors the author-time Markdown tokenizer (CMH-HL-07) with the same token mapping, so an unbaked `<pre><code class="language-markdown">` block self-heals on load with headings, emphasis, links, code spans, lists and fenced blocks colored, and a `.md` / `.markdown` / `.mkd` file in a unified diff is highlighted from its filename (`_EXT_LANG`). | CMH-HL-09 | Every token-highlighted code block - in any language, KQL included - is reversible: `dehighlight()` recovers the exact source the highlighter was given, over the newline-normalized domain (both emitters fold CRLF and lone CR to LF, so the inverse is a LEFT inverse, not byte-exact recovery of arbitrary input). For content ALREADY stored highlighted, which is the only thing an edit loop round-trips, newlines are already LF and so dehighlight followed by re-highlight is byte-identical - an untouched block never churns bytes. Escaped entities in the source (`&amp;`, `&lt;`), a literal `</span>` inside a string, multi-line tokens (docstrings, block comments, KQL `@"..."` verbatim strings), tabs, blank runs and astral Unicode all survive the round trip. `dehighlight()` ends in an unescape and must therefore be applied to stored inner HTML exactly once. | `tests/test_highlight_core.py` - `DehighlightLeftInverseTests` (`test_code_round_trip_recovers_normalized_source`, `test_kql_round_trip_recovers_normalized_source`, `test_crlf_is_normalized_not_preserved`, `test_rehighlight_of_stored_content_is_byte_identical`, `test_kql_rehighlight_of_stored_content_is_byte_identical`, `test_empty_and_whitespace_only_blocks`); source: `tools/blocks/_highlight_core.py` - `dehighlight()`, `normalize_newlines()` |
| CMH-HL-10 | The inverse is a strict SINGLE-PASS scanner over the generated grammar, so content the emitters did not produce is refused rather than corrupted. Only an exact `<span class="cmh-{code,kql}-KIND">` with a kind on the emitter's own allowlist, no other attributes, no nesting and a balanced close is recognized; because every emitter escapes all of `&`, `<` and `>`, a correctly generated inner holds no literal angle bracket and is canonically escaped, so any surviving `<` or `>` after the pass - or any non-canonical entity the emitters never write (`&quot;`, `&#x3C;`, `&eacute;`, a bare `&`) - proves the block is hand-written, nested, malformed, or carries an unknown token kind, and `dehighlight()` returns `None`. The exact-escaping rule also makes accidental DOUBLE application refuse instead of silently decoding source that legitimately contains `&amp;`. A repeated-substitution loop is specifically NOT used: it would peel nested spans from the inside out and hand back plausible but corrupted source, silently defeating the refusal. `classify()` reports `raw`, `highlighted`, or `hand-written` so callers can pass a hand-written block through untouched instead of stalling on it. | `tests/test_highlight_core.py` - `StrictScannerTests` (`test_nested_spans_are_refused_not_unwound`, `test_author_markup_is_refused`, `test_malformed_span_is_refused`, `test_unknown_token_class_is_refused`, `test_non_canonical_escaping_is_refused`, `test_double_application_is_refused_rather_than_corrupting`, `test_entity_bearing_source_still_round_trips`, `test_raw_escaped_text_is_accepted`, `test_highlighted_content_classifies_as_highlighted`); source: `tools/blocks/_highlight_core.py` - `classify()`, `_TOKEN_SPAN_RE`, `_is_canonically_escaped()` |
| CMH-HL-11 | The code highlighter and the KQL highlighter share ONE emission point (`esc()` / `span()` in `tools/blocks/_highlight_core.py`), one exact inverse (`unesc()`) and one newline normalizer, so the inverse provably covers every language rather than being reimplemented per tokenizer. Emitter output is asserted FLAT (no span ever nests inside another), which is the property the single-pass inverse depends on, and the token-kind allowlist is asserted to cover every kind the emitters actually emit, so a future tokenizer change that introduced nesting or a new kind fails here instead of silently breaking every caller. | `tests/test_highlight_core.py` - `FlatnessTests` (`test_emitter_output_is_never_nested`, `test_both_emitters_use_the_shared_span`, `test_the_kind_allowlist_covers_every_kind_the_emitters_emit`, `test_unesc_is_the_exact_inverse_of_esc`, `test_markdown_fuzz_stays_flat_and_reversible`); source: `tools/blocks/_highlight_core.py` - `esc()`, `unesc()`, `span()`, `is_flat()`, `CODE_KINDS`, `KQL_KINDS`; `tools/blocks/highlight_code.py`, `tools/kusto/kql_highlight.py` |

| CMH-KQL-05 | The validator warns when a `cmh-kql-run` link is not an HTTPS ADX link, or opens an AUXILIARY browsing context without `rel="noopener"`. Both operands are read the way a browser reads them: the `rel` list is tokenized on ASCII whitespace ONLY, through the shared `link_rel_tokens` every other `rel` reader uses, and the `target` is the EFFECTIVE one HTML resolves, through the shared `effective_link_target` the render-time stamper (CMH-LINK-01) also reads - an anchor with no `target` of its own inherits the document's FIRST `<base target>` (a later one is ignored, as HTML ignores it; and the `<base>` is the one a BROWSER applies - the lookup runs off the namespace-aware document parser, so a `<base>` parked in an inert `<template>` or a declarative shadow root, or written under `<svg>`/`<math>`, decides nothing, where a raw name scan let one written before the real base mask it), and a name carrying BOTH an ASCII tab-or-newline and a U+003C is coerced to `_blank` (the coercion runs after the base lookup, so an inherited value is coerced too; both characters are required). That effective value is then matched against HTML's four keywords ASCII case-insensitively and UNTRIMMED, so anything that CREATES an auxiliary browsing context - `_BLANK`, a padded ` _blank`, an inherited `<base target="_blank">`, a coerced `x&#10;<`, or a NAME that resolves to nothing in this document - hands the opened page a live `window.opener`. Only an HTML anchor INHERITS (HTML's rule is defined for an HTML `a`/`area`/`form`), so a foreign run link is never warned about for a base it cannot inherit. The named-context EXEMPTION is read the same browser-accurate way: only a LIVE HTML `<iframe>`/`<frame>`/`<object name>` declares a context, so a frame parked in a `<template>`, a declarative shadow root, or foreign content no longer makes an unresolvable name look resolvable. The warning names the AUTHORED markup and the rule that transformed it (`target=...` / `inherited <base target>=...`, each with a `, which HTML coerces to ...` clause when it applies), so an author is never sent looking for an attribute their document does not contain. A name that DOES resolve (an `<iframe name="win1">` written in the same document) navigates a context that already exists, gets no opener, and is exempt: warning there would be a false positive, and taking the advice would change behavior, since `noopener` stops a named target reusing the frame. The keywords are checked FIRST, so a frame named `_blank` cannot silence the gate. Python's argument-less `str.split()` also splits on the vertical tab U+000B, NBSP and U+001C-U+001F, so `rel="noopener<VT>x"` used to name the token `noopener` and pass the gate while a browser saw ONE opaque relation, left `window.opener` exposed, and let the opened page navigate the document the reader is looking at; and a Python `==` against the literal `_blank` missed every other opener-keeping spelling entirely, so a link carrying no `rel` at all passed; reading the RAW attribute likewise missed an inherited `<base target>` and the `<`-coercion (#1141). The warning names the AUTHORED markup and the rule that transformed it, so an author whose link carries no `target` at all is not sent looking for an attribute that is not there. That matters here more than elsewhere because this gate is the ONLY reverse-tabnabbing control on a run link: CMH-KQL-01 places it inside `figcaption.cm-skip`, which both the render-time stamper (CMH-LINK-01) and the `checks/links.py` new-tab check skip. The ORIGIN half asks CMH-KQL-07's question through CMH-KQL-07's predicate (`_is_adx_run_href`) rather than restating it as a literal `https://dataexplorer.azure.com/` prefix test on the raw href. That prefix was the FALSE-POSITIVE direction of the same class of defect - case-sensitive and path-bound, so `HTTPS://DataExplorer.Azure.Com/x`, `https://dataexplorer.azure.com:443/x`, `https://dataexplorer.azure.com?q` and a bare `https://dataexplorer.azure.com` all warned, which `--strict` turns into a hard failure, about links a browser really does open in ADX. The swap only ever REMOVES warnings: the prefix pins the authority exactly, so every href it accepted the parse accepts too, and the one spelling it warned about that a parse could have cleared - a non-default port - is an origin the predicate refuses as well.
